They continued (p-43) until they caught up with them at the Sea of al-Qulzum, as the explanation of that was given earlier in al-A'raf from the Torah, and the secret of their being directed along that route was also mentioned earlier.

When the two hosts came in sight of each other, that is, they came to a position where each saw the other, the companions of Moses said, out of weakness and helplessness, carrying over the humiliation they had been in among them: "Indeed we are surely overtaken." This is because they had arrived, and there was no way out for us, and we are now between two barriers, of iron and water: the enemy behind us and the water in front of us.

Also, they were far fewer in number than them, to the extent that it is said that the vanguard of the people of Pharaoh was equal in number to the Children of Israel, and that is correct, since Pharaoh had made them few. It seems that he referred to them as "the companions" rather than "the Children of Israel" because many others had also believed among them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 62:

﴿Qāla﴾ (He said): i.e., Musa, upon him be peace, trusting in the promise of Allah, speaking the same words his Lord had spoken to him at the beginning of the story, in His saying: ﴿Kallā﴾ (By no means!), i.e., they will not overtake you at all. Then he gave a reason for this, to calm them, with his saying: ﴿Inna maʿiya Rabbī﴾ (Indeed, my Lord is with me). It is as if they said: "And what can He do, now that they have reached us?" So he said: ﴿Sayahdīni﴾ (He will guide me), i.e., with a firmly affirmed promise, soon, to what I should do of that which brings about your deliverance. The secret of placing the "with me" (maʿiyya) first, its specificity, and the expression by the name of the Lord (Rabb) was discussed earlier in Surat Barā'a (al-Tawba).

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 63:**

﴿Then We revealed﴾ meaning: thus, as a consequence of his speech which indicated reliance (al-muraqabah, watchfulness over God), We revealed; and He honoured him by his noble name as a reward for his trust [in] Him, glorified is He, so He said: ﴿to Moses﴾. He explained the revelation, which contains the meaning of speech, by His saying: ﴿Strike the sea with your staff﴾, meaning: the sea that is before you, which is the Sea of Qulzum (Red Sea), through which the people of Egypt reach Sinai (al-Tur), Mecca the Honoured, and what surrounds them. ﴿So it parted﴾, meaning: he struck it and it split [because of his striking], when he struck it in compliance with God's command, and it became twelve paths according to the number of their tribes (asbat). ﴿And each portion was﴾, meaning: each part and great section of it, ﴿like a mountain﴾, meaning: a mountain in its height, its length, and its firmness, not flowing away, ﴿great﴾, stretching up into the sky, firm and not shaking. This is because the water had been spread out over the bed of the sea; when it split [and the paths were opened within it], some of it joined with other parts, so it grew tall and rose into the sky.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 64:

As the sense was: "So We made every group of them enter a path among those paths," he followed it with: ﴿And We brought near﴾, i.e., We brought near, by Our greatness, the people of Musa, peace be upon him; so said al-Baghawi. Abu 'Ubayda said: "We gathered together" (jama'na), and from this comes the Night of Muzdalifa (laylat al-muzdalifa), i.e., the Night of Gathering (laylat al-jam').

Since this gathering was at the utmost of greatness and elevated rank, he indicated it with the particle of distance, saying: ﴿There﴾, i.e., "over there," for it is a locative adverb (zarf makan) for what is far away,

﴿the others﴾, i.e., Pharaoh and his hosts.

And We delivered Moses and those with him, all of them. ﴿And We delivered Moses and all who were with him﴾ — they are those who followed him from his people and others — ﴿all of them﴾, i.e., We did not decree destruction upon any of them.

Since the drowning, together with the means by which the deliverance was achieved, was a fearsome matter yet also strange and remote, He expressed it with the particle of distance, saying: ﴿Then We drowned the others﴾. That is, a drowning befitting Our greatness, [drowning] ﴿the others﴾, namely Pharaoh and his people, all of them, of whom not one escaped.

When Moses's plea, which he made at the beginning of the story to ward off Pharaoh's scheming, was established by the greatness and power that were proven for him, through the multitude of the soldiers and their great obedience to him in gathering quickly, which indicates their power over themselves and his greatness in their hearts, out of desire and dread; and the glory of God appeared in fulfilling what He, glorified is He, had promised of protection, and it increased what gladdened the eyes and expanded the breasts; and that was a matter whose hearing shakes the faculties and whose imagining and mention startles the ears—He said, drawing attention to that: ﴿Indeed in that﴾, that is, in the great matter of high rank from the story of Moses and Pharaoh and what it contains of lessons, ﴿is surely a sign﴾, that is, a great sign, according to what the Messenger said, obligating belief in it: that the Creator is one, a free agent by choice, able over everything, and that he is truly His messenger. ﴿And most of them were not believers﴾, that is, those who witnessed it and those who were admonished by hearing it, ﴿believers﴾, that is, characterized by firm faith. As for the Copts, none of them believed except the magicians, the believer of Pharaoh's family, and Pharaoh's wife, and the woman who guided them to the bones of Joseph, peace be upon him—according to what is said. As for the Children of Israel, many of them were unsteady, complaining every little while, saying and doing what is disbelief, until God, exalted is He, rectified them through Moses, peace be upon him, and those after him. The first of that was their request, right after crossing the sea, that He make for them a god like the idols they had passed by. As for others who came after them, their state is well known and their affair is evident and manifest.

Surely your Lord is the One who shows favour to you by exalting your cause and rescuing people from the darkness of ignorance at your hands. ﴿Indeed, He is the Almighty﴾, that is, the One able to take vengeance upon every wicked sinner, ﴿the Most Merciful﴾, that is, the One who acts with the utmost mercy. He gives respite, and bestows abundant blessings, and shields from retribution, and does not leave people unguided; rather, He sends messengers, and sends down with them that by which He makes clear what pleases Him and what angers Him, so no one is destroyed except after the establishment of proof. Therefore, do not feel desolate on account of those who do not believe, and let that not trouble you.

When Allah, glory be to Him, had completed what He intended of the story of Musa, peace be upon him, He followed it, as a proof of His mercy, with the story of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. This is because of what preceded: that Ibrahim shared with Musa in what consoles (the Prophet) regarding what was mentioned of their stubborn demands (ta'annut) in the Furqan (the Criterion, i.e., the Qur'an). It is also because Ibrahim was singled out for confronting his father and his people over the idols, and he is the greatest of the fathers of the Arabs. This is so that the story would move them to follow him in monotheism (tawhid) if they cannot part with imitation (taqlid), and so that it would deter them from regarding it as grave to call their fathers foolish for worshipping the idols. His glory's choice of wording suits the context before and after. His saying ﴿Recite﴾, i.e., read in continuous succession, favors the first interpretation of "wa-idh" as meaning "remember," which is the view that makes it "udhkur" (remember). His change of wording with it suits the context of what came before and what comes after, to alert the Arabs to follow him, because of the special relationship they have with him. ﴿Upon them﴾, i.e., upon these people who are deluded by the idols and who deny that a human can be a messenger. ﴿The news of Ibrahim﴾, i.e., his great account in such a matter.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 26, verse 70:

﴿When﴾, that is, at the time when ﴿he said to his father and his people﴾, admonishing them for their misguidance, not seeking information, since he knew the reality of their condition: ﴿"What"﴾ [that is:] which thing, [and their condition was depicted to them to alert them to its ugliness, so he expressed it in the present tense, saying:] ﴿"do you worship?"﴾, that is, do you persist in worshipping it?

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 26, verse 71:**

﴿They said﴾, delighted at his question and showing pride in their answer by lengthening their speech: ﴿We worship idols, and so we remain﴾, meaning: as a consequence of our worship of them, we fulfil the right of worship by persisting ﴿devoted to them﴾, meaning: circling around them continuously, one of us following behind another in ranks, restraining ourselves out of reverence (p. 48) for them. They followed the example of these people in the *dā'* (disease) of *taqlīd* (blind imitation), which arises from ignorance of the very nature of worship. They also believed, along with this, that they were upon a great gain and a momentous matter, which they had attained, while the creation was heedless of it. This is what their speech in this statement indicates, which could have dispensed with it in a single word. This is also what required interpreting *ẓalla* (﴿fa-naẓallu﴾) in the sense of mere continuance, even though its meaning is continuance restricted to daytime. It seems they intended, by what indicates daytime, which is the place of occupation and wakefulness, to indicate night by a fortiori reasoning, along with the wide usage of the word in an unrestricted sense, as in ﴿then their necks remained humbled before them﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 4]. [The people of Abraham, peace be upon him, added that they persisted in their error, and his father was with them, so they became fuel for the Fire. He was unable to rescue them from that, and they had no recourse except his supplication. So he is most deserving of intense grief and of consuming himself with sorrow over them, and this is the place of consolation.]

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 72:

When this desire was understood from them, he began to dissuade them from it by way of *istifham* (interrogation), the most just form of questioning, concerning attributes. The question compels them to acknowledge that these attributes are negated of them, while every intelligent person, when he reflects, knows that the station of divinity cannot be valid with the lack of even one of them, so how much less with the lack of all of them. Thus God, the Exalted, reports about him, saying: ﴿He [Abraham] said﴾, referring to them in the manner used for rational beings, out of fairness, by treating them as though they occupied that station: (p-49) ﴿Do they hear you﴾, i.e., your supplication, with mere hearing. Then he depicted their state to them so that they would be restrained from pondering it. He said, expressing it with a past temporal adverb (*ẓarf*) and a present-tense verb, ﴿when you call﴾, to draw attention to the bringing together of all of time, so that this would be more forceful in rebuke (*tabkit*). I.e., recall your circumstances with them from the beginning of your worship of them until now: did they ever hear you at any time? This would give you hope of obtaining some benefit from them at some time.

Since a person may devote himself to a thing even though it cannot hear, either for its benefit to him personally or for its harm to his enemy, like fire for example, and since the primary aim of the worshipper and the supplicant is, in essence and first of all, the attainment of benefit, He said: ﴿Or do they benefit you﴾, i.e., by worship, just as the least thing you possess benefits you, ﴿or do they harm﴾, by abandonment.

They said: "No, by Allah! They had nothing of that." Rather, "We found our fathers doing so" (﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾), meaning: like our present act of exalted rank. Then they pictured the state of their fathers in their own minds, magnifying their affair, and said: ﴿يَفْعَلُونَ﴾ ("they do"), meaning: we do as they did, because they have a claim on us that we not oppose them, given that they preceded us into existence. They are firmer of intellect than us and greater in experience. So had they not seen that practice as good, they would not have persisted in it. [This is so] even though, if they had followed a path grounded in the senses that brought them some sensory harm, they would never have followed it at all. But this religion makes imitation of falsehood easy for people, in the past and in the present.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 75:

When they reached mere imitation (taqlid), devoid of even the slightest reflection, just as cattle and birds follow their first of kind, ﴿He said﴾, turning away from answering their words with censure, as an indication that their words are worthless and not to be approved by anyone who has smelled the scent of manliness: ﴿Have you considered﴾, meaning: so from your saying this I say to you, "Have you considered?", that is, if you have not seen them with a sight that establishes the reality of their condition, then look at them with a thorough look, ﴿what you have been﴾, meaning: in a state that has become like a disposition in you, ﴿worshipping﴾, persisting in their worship.

﴿You﴾.

When they answered him with taqlid (uncritical imitation of ancestral tradition), he said to them, meaning: "Carry this taqlid of yours to its furthest extent, for precedence and priority are not a proof of correctness, and falsehood does not turn into truth through antiquity. This is what he intends by His words: ﴿and your forefathers of old﴾, i.e., those who are the most ancient of all: Do they possess any attribute other than what you have acknowledged (p. 51) of not hearing, benefiting, or harming?"

Then he began to describe Him by what they themselves know: that He is at the utmost opposite of everything their idols are. So He said: ﴿Who﴾. And since no one claimed to create, He had no need for anything indicating exclusivity, so He said: ﴿created me﴾, that is, brought me into existence in the form of measuring and shaping (p. 52). ﴿Then He﴾, that is, as a consequence of His sole creation of me, He alone and no other ﴿guides me﴾, that is, to right guidance. And because no one other than the Creator knows the inner reality of the created being and can exercise complete control over it, [and the one who creates him must be All-Hearing, All-Seeing, Able to harm and to benefit, possessing all perfection. There is no doubt that creation pertains to the body and guidance to the spirit, and through creation and guidance all benefits are attained. The human being has a frame from the world of creation and a frame from the world of command, and the composition of the frame takes precedence,] as becomes apparent from this verse, [and as in His saying: ﴿So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit﴾ (Q. 15:29), and similar passages. He mentioned creation in the past tense because it does not recur in this world, and guidance in the present tense because it is renewed and repeated, in religion and in worldly life.]

﴿And He who​ it is﴾, i.e., none other than Him, ﴿Who feeds me and gives me drink﴾, and if He willed, He could deprive me of what I eat and what I drink, or afflict me with a calamity by which I would be unable to eat or drink.

Since sickness is a harm, he (Abraham) attributed it not to God out of courtesy (adab), although the attribution of everything to Him, glorified is He, is known. He said: ﴿And when I am sick﴾ through the dominance of some humors over others, because of the natural antagonism between them, ﴿it is He﴾ that is, He alone, ﴿who heals me﴾ by means of restoring the balance of the temperament through adjusting the humors and compelling them to unite and remain in equilibrium—not a physician nor anyone else, even though I may be the cause of my own illnesses through cold or heat, or food I eat, or other things, because He is capable of whatever He wills.

(p-53) Since man is naturally disposed to strive to preserve his life and the survival of his soul, He attributed the act of causing death to Himself, out of magnification of power, saying: ﴿And who causes me to die﴾, that is, physically, even if I strive to ward off death, and in meaning, even if I strive to ward off ignorance.

Since giving life, both physically through the spirit and in meaning through guidance, is a great matter, He used the particle of delay for it, and for the long stay in the *barzakh* (the intermediate realm between death and resurrection), saying: ﴿then will bring me to life﴾, for recompense in the Hereafter, as He healed me from illness, even if I reached a state in which I was not expected to recover. He did not state here anything that indicates restriction [not], because there is no claimant to giving life and causing death except what He, glorified is He, mentioned about Nimrod in Surat al-Baqarah, and that Abraham (peace be upon him) silenced him by demonstrating his inability to produce an image in some place among places, without any condition of a spirit or otherwise. If he is unable to do that, then his inability to create an image is clearer. How much more so when there is added to that conferring a spirit upon it or taking it away from it. So his claim to that, along with the clear sensory proof that silenced him, is counted as nothing. And God knows best.

When he mentioned the resurrection, he mentioned what follows from it, so he said: ﴿And the One from whom I hope﴾, humbling himself, abasing his own deeds, and indicating that, in relation to the Supreme Presence (al-Ḥaḍrah al-Aʿẓamiyyah), he is not capable of giving it its due worth. For hope (ṭamaʿ), as al-Ḥirālī said in (his commentary on) al-Baqarah (p-54), is the attachment of the heart to a thing without any prior cause, end quote. Therefore he did not prepare any deed for it. ﴿that He will forgive﴾, i.e., erase and cover.

Since God, glory be to Him, is exalted above having a purpose, and forgiveness is only for the benefit of the servant, he said: ﴿me﴾, and he attributed the sin to himself, humbling himself and showing humility [before his Lord, so he said]: ﴿my sin﴾, i.e., my shortcoming in not estimating Him as He deserves to be estimated. For the weak and incapable does not reach all that is due in the service of the Exalted, the Great. And what he did is by His empowering, glory be to Him, so in reality he has no doing at all. ﴿on the Day of Judgment﴾, i.e., the recompense.

When he had praised God, Exalted is He, with what is due to Him, and concluded with mention of this great Day, he prayed for what would ward off its terror. His conduct shows that putting praise before request is an important matter and has a great effect on being answered. So he said, turning to the station of witnessing, to indicate that the matter is awesome and that none can rescue from its peril except the One of great power, because of the deficiencies the soul is created with: ﴿My Lord﴾, i.e., O You who have been good to me; ﴿grant me hukm (wisdom)﴾, i.e., a deed perfected with knowledge. Its root meaning is building a thing according to what wisdom requires. Since reliance is only upon pure generosity, for whoever is called to a strict reckoning is punished, he said: ﴿and join me with the righteous﴾, i.e., those whom You made imams for the God-fearing in this world and the Hereafter, who are those whose speech and action are free of any admixture of corruption. (p-٥٥)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 84:

Since the righteous person's good deeds may not become apparent, and since God's making them apparent is a means of attracting supplication and an increase in reward, He said: ﴿Grant me a tongue of truthfulness﴾, meaning: a good remembrance, general acceptance, and a fine praise, by means of what You have made apparent in me of the qualities of goodness, ﴿among the later ones﴾, meaning: the people who will exist after me until the Day of Judgment, so that I may be an imam (leader) for the God-fearing (al-muttaqun), and so that I may have a like share of their rewards. For, "Whoever establishes a good sunnah (practice) will have its reward and the reward of whoever acts upon it until the Day of Resurrection." And this was an answer from God Most High to his supplication. Among the greatest of it is that God made him a blessed tree, from which He brought forth the prophets, through whom his remembrance was revived, peace be upon them all. Among the greatest of that remembrance is what was upon the tongue of the greatest of them, the Unlettered Prophet (ﷺ), in his saying: "O God, send blessings upon Muhammad as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim," to its end.

Since he sought the felicity of this world, and it had no benefit except through its connection with the felicity of the Hereafter, which is the Garden (al-Jannah), and the Garden cannot be attained except by His bounty (mannihi), not by anything of that kind, for this reason he likened its entry to the inheritance that comes about without acquisition by the heir, and that is the strongest of the causes of sovereignty. He said: ﴿And make me﴾, that is: in addition to all of that (p-56) by Your grace and Your mercy, ﴿among the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss﴾.

When he had prayed for himself, he followed with the one most deserving of his dutiful kindness, saying: ﴿And forgive my father﴾. Then he gave the reason for his prayer with his words: ﴿Indeed, he was among the astray﴾ during the days of his life. And the apparent meaning is that this was before he knew of the everlasting (ta'bid) of his wretchedness, and for this reason he said it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 87:

﴿And do not disgrace me﴾, i.e., do not humiliate me by (the fate of) his (my father's) death in a state that necessitates his entry into the Fire, nor by anything else. ﴿On the day they are resurrected﴾, i.e., these deniers of the Resurrection. It seems that this supplication was made in the presence of them while he was denouncing them for worshipping idols. The apparent view is that the supplication was specifically for his father because his mother had believed, as has been related from ...

"It is authentically reported that he will say on the Day of Resurrection: 'My Lord! You promised me that You would not disgrace me. What disgrace could be greater than (that of) my farthest father?' Then Allah will change the form of his father into the form of a hyena (dhikh), and then cast him into the Fire, as al-Bukhari related in more than one place from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), and that Allah the Exalted will say to him: 'Indeed I have forbidden Paradise to the disbelievers.' Had (his father) been a disbelieving mother, he would have asked Him about her."

Once he had alerted us that the true aim is the Hereafter, he made the renunciation of this world explicit by belittling its most prized things, so he said: ﴿The Day when neither wealth nor sons will benefit﴾, that is, benefit anyone, ﴿wealth﴾, that is, (p-57) by which one might ransom oneself [with it], or give it to an intercessor or to a mighty helper who overpowers, ﴿nor sons﴾, by whom one might gain victory or find support, so how much less anything else.

﴿Except for one who comes to God﴾, i.e., the Greatest King, who alone holds absolute sufficiency on this occasion, ﴿with a sound heart﴾, i.e., one free from the sickness that has altered it from the original nature (fitrah) upon which God created it. This original nature is Islam, whose foundation is monotheism (tawhid), steadfastness in doing good, and preserving the path of the Sunnah, just as a beast gives birth to a complete beast with no mutilated part in it. For ﴿wealth and children﴾ [al-Kahf 18:46] benefit him by whatever good he spends on them. The exception here is an exceptive construction with no stated object (istithna' mufarragh). The apparent meaning of His saying

And the Garden is brought near to the God-fearing (﴿وأُزْلِفَتِ الجَنَّةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾). That is, it is drought near, ... 

Let me restate carefully and fully to match the source text.

"And the Garden was brought near (﴿وأُزْلِفَتِ﴾), i.e., it was brought close in the easiest manner, as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the waw of "yubʿathūn" (they are resurrected) — ﴿al-Jannatu lil-muttaqīn﴾ (the Garden is for the God-fearing). He made known to the people of the standing place (ahl al-mawqif) that it is specifically theirs, in order to hasten their joy and to increase them in honor."

"And Hellfire was brought forth" — i.e., it was uncovered, with a great and easy uncovering — "al-Jahim" — i.e., the fire of intense blazing; its origin is a great fire in a deep pit, some of it above others — "for those who go astray" — i.e., the misguided, the ruined, in such a way that the people of the place of standing knew that it was for them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 92:

﴿And it will be said to them﴾ as rebuke, reproach and censure; and he left the speaker unspecified so that it would fit everyone, as a way of belittling them, and because what causes the rebuke is the saying itself, not that it comes from a specific person: ﴿Where is what you used to﴾ worship, by adopting dispositions that have become like innate natures ﴿worship﴾, i.e. (p-58) in the world, in a manner of renewal and continuity.

He belittled their objects of worship by His saying: ﴿Other than﴾ [i.e., from any lowest rank among the ranks] ﴿Allah﴾, i.e., the King who has no equal, and you used to claim that they would intercede for you and shield you from the evil of this Day. ﴿Can they help you﴾ by warding off from you what has come upon you? ﴿Or can they defend themselves?﴾ i.e., by repelling [harm] from themselves.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 94:

When this exposure and speech had as their consequence the manifestation of His power, exalted is He, and their incapacity through their being cast into it, He said: ﴿Then they will be thrown headlong into it﴾, i.e., the idols and the like were overturned, cast down and hurled, a great, repeated, swift overturning [from everyone whom Allah commanded to overturn them] after this question, a manifestation of their incapacity in deed, even before answering. ﴿Into it﴾, i.e., into the abyss of Hellfire, an intense, multiplied overturning, many of them one after another. ﴿They﴾, i.e., the idols and what resembles them of those worshipped apart from Allah, such as devils and the like. ﴿And the deviators﴾, i.e., those who went astray because of them.
﴿And the hosts of Iblis, all of them﴾ from the devils of mankind and of the jinn ﴿all of them﴾

When this became known, that they could not produce an answer to their question as a rebuke, and since it is well known that a person is naturally disposed to say, about anything that befalls him, whatever his perception prompts him to say, what he sees as cooling his thirst and benefiting his ailment, the listener became eager [to know] what they would say after the *kabkaba* (the headlong hurling into the Fire). This is indicated by His words (p-٥٩) ﴿They will say﴾, i.e., the worshippers, ﴿while they are therein﴾, i.e., in the Blazing Fire, ﴿quarrelling﴾, i.e., with the objects of worship.
"By Allah" — that is, the One who possesses all perfection — "Indeed, we were in clear error" — that is, evident to a great degree to anyone who has a heart.
﴿When﴾ means: at the time when ﴿We make you equal﴾ in rank ﴿to the Lord of the worlds﴾, meaning those whom He originated and governed, until we worshipped you.

"And none led us astray except the criminals", that is, that manifest misguidance from the clear path. "Except the criminals": that is, those deeply rooted (ʿarīqūn) in the attribute of criminality (ijrām), which necessitates severing everything that ought to be connected.

Then, as a consequence of that, [they say] that they have no ﴿intercessors﴾ today. They intensified the negation by adding the preposition, saying ﴿from intercessors﴾ who would be a cause of our entry into the Garden, because we diverted what was obligatory upon us toward those who had the command to those who have no command. Perhaps the singular "intercessor" was not used because they entered into the great intercession.

When the friend may not be fit to intercede, they said, lamenting over the least that could be hoped for: ﴿Nor a friend﴾, that is, one who is sincere in his affection for us so as to do what benefits us. And since the truest friendship is that of a close relative, he said: ﴿a close friend (ḥamīm)﴾, that is, a kinsman. Its root is the pure one (al-maṣāfī), the one whose burning is the same as your burning. We have cut off by this every person who has any concern on this Day. He used the singular to express generality in negation, and as an indication of its scarcity in itself or its non-existence.

(p-60) When they had fallen into this destruction, and no deliverance remained for them, there followed from it their wishing for the impossible, and they said: ﴿So that we might have a return (karrah)﴾, that is, a return to the world, ﴿and then we would be among the believers﴾, that is, those for whom faith has become a constant attribute. Then Paradise was brought near to them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 103:

Since this story contains the greatest deterrent from shirk (associating partners with God), and commands belief in faith, he drew attention to this by His saying: ﴿Indeed in that﴾, i.e., this great matter which I have related of the words of Ibrahim, upon him be peace, in establishing the proof for the invalidity of idols, and setting up the evidence that none has right [to worship] except the Sovereign, the Majestic, the Judge, and [of] his encouragement, his warning, and his guidance to provisioning oneself during the days of respite, ﴿is surely a sign﴾, i.e., a great sign of the falsity of falsehood and the rightness of truth; ﴿yet most of them are not believers﴾, i.e., while the state is that most of those who witnessed this great matter from him and those who heard of it from him were not ﴿believers﴾, i.e., such that faith became a firm attribute of theirs. In that is the greatest consolation for the Prophet ﷺ, through the greatest of his forefathers, upon them be blessings and peace.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 104:

﴿And indeed, your Lord﴾ — that is, the One who is good to you by sending you and guiding the community through you — ﴿is surely the All-Mighty﴾ — that is, the One able to inflict vengeance upon everyone who opposes Him when they oppose Him — ﴿the Most Merciful﴾ — that is, the One who acts as one who is merciful in granting respite to the disobedient while showering blessings, warding off retribution, sending messengers, and establishing laws, to clarify what He is pleased with so that it may be followed, and what angers Him so that it may be avoided. (p-61) So He does not destroy except after establishing proof by making the path clear.

When the Exalted One had completed the story of the Greatest and Nearest Father, He followed it, as a sign of the attributes of might and mercy, with the story of the second father, placing it before the others because of its antiquity in time, to inform that trial is ancient, and because it is more indicative of the attributes of mercy and vengeance, which are the effect of might, through the prolonged respite granted to them over the length of their time, and then the generalization of vengeance, since they were all the people of the earth. So He said: ﴿The people of Nuh denied the messengers﴾, with the feminine ta' (kadhdhabat) retained by choice for the feminine gender, although the masculine form (for "the people") is more common, to alert to the fact that their act was the basest of acts [or, to indicate that, despite their obstinacy and great numbers, they were before Him, glorified be He, the most insignificant and weakest of things, to the point that He made them scattered dust, and likewise those who came after them]. ﴿The people of Nuh﴾: they were the whole of the people of the earth from among the children of Adam before the differentiation of nations through the dispersion of languages. ﴿The messengers﴾: that is, by their denial of Nuh, peace be upon him, because he established the proof of his prophethood through a miracle, and whoever denies one miracle has denied all miracles, since their proofs are equal in indicating the truthfulness of the Messenger. Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, was asked about this and said: "Whoever denies one of the messengers has denied them all, because the later one came with what the first one came with." Al-Baghawi related this from him.

For the sake of consolation, he expressed the denial in every story [with the word "takdhib"]. ﴿When﴾, that is, when ﴿he said to them﴾, they did not trouble themselves to seek proof, nor to seek a fair manner of address. He pointed to his kinship with them by his words ﴿their brother﴾, increasing the consolation of this noble Prophet (p-62) ﴿Noah﴾. He also pointed to the goodness of his manners and his winning them over by his gentleness and softness, through his words ﴿Will you not fear God?﴾, that is: that you may have taqwa (God-consciousness), which is a fear that moves you to place between yourselves and His wrath a shield (wiqayah) by obeying Him through monotheism and abandoning the turning toward anything other than Him.

Then he gave the reason for his fitness to command them by his saying: ﴿Indeed, I am to you﴾ [i.e., ] while I am your brother, I am troubled by what troubles you and gladdened by what gladdens you, ﴿a messenger﴾, i.e., from the presence of your Creator, so there is no escape for me from conveying what I have been commanded, ﴿trustworthy﴾, i.e., there is no deceit in me, as you know this of me through your long experience of me, and no betrayal in any part of the trust; therefore it is necessary for me to convey the whole message.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 108:

When he presented piety to them gently, and gave as the reason for it that by which its command was established, there followed from this a firm command, so he said: ﴿So fear God﴾, that is: bring about fear, caution and guarding yourselves against the One who is singled out for majesty and beauty, hastening toward that by affirming His oneness, so that you secure the root of happiness and thus become among the people of Paradise. ﴿And obey me﴾, that is: in everything I command you, so that you secure the rank of perfection in that, and then no punishment will touch you.

Once he had established his trustworthiness, he negated the accusation against him, saying: ﴿And I do not ask you any reward for it﴾, i.e., for this state in which I have come to you. He indicated the thoroughness of the negation by his saying: ﴿any reward﴾ [i.e.,] so that a suspecting person might suppose that I made the invocation a means to it. Then (p-63) he emphasized this negation by his saying: "in" (ان), i.e., my reward ﴿is not but from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [meaning] in my supplication for you, i.e., the One who governs and nurtures all creation.

When the accusation was removed, there followed from its removal also what he had mentioned earlier, so he repeated it, informing them of his concern for this, increasing in compassion toward them [and emphasizing it in their hearts, as a reminder that the matter is of the utmost greatness, because of what is known of their hearts in terms of extreme coarseness]. So he said: ﴿So fear Allah﴾, that is, the One who possesses all the attributes of greatness, ﴿and obey me﴾.

When the evidence for his sincere counsel and trustworthiness was established, they answered with something that looks only at the mere worldly life, as one of the noble Arabs did when he said, ﴿What is wrong with this Messenger?﴾ [al-Furqan: 7], and the verses that follow it. He also said, "If you drove away these weak ones, we would hope to follow you," until there was revealed concerning that ﴿Do not drive away those who call upon their Lord﴾ [al-An'am: 52] and similar verses. Thus ﴿they said﴾, that is, his people, denying that they would follow him, relying on the disease of arrogance from which comes rejection of the truth and contempt for people (ghamt al-nas), that is, looking down on them: ﴿Shall we believe you?﴾, that is, on account of this statement of yours and the qualities you have claimed for yourself, ﹘"and" the situation is that ﹘"the lowliest have followed you," that is, those who are behind in their state and their outcome, in their conditions and their actions. So our belief in you would be a cause of our being made equal with them. Then, if you drove them away, we would have no excuse for lagging behind you, and nothing would prevent us from following you. So what they were given of fleeting worldly goods became an obstacle preventing them from lasting happiness. As for the weak, their hearts are broken and empty of any preoccupation that would turn them toward good and make them accept it, because God, exalted is He, is near to hearts that are broken. Thus Quraysh said about the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), and the followers of the messengers continued to be like this until it became one of their marks and signs, as Heraclius said when he asked about the followers of the Prophet (ﷺ). The example of the arrogant is the example of a person who had another beneath him by one rank, then found himself one rank above him. He was too proud to rise to the other's rank lest he become equal to him, and he was content for himself to remain below him. How foolish his intellect is! How great his ignorance is! Nothing is clearer than this in showing that precedence in worldly affairs is a disease for which there is no cure except the killing of the self by disowning it and keeping far from it.

(p-64)

Since precious stones are all equal in being creations of God, and are only honored by their effects, so a human being is honored or debased only by his state, by his words and his deeds, he indicated that what matters is only their present high conditions and wondrous attributes. Therefore ﴿He said﴾, denying knowledge of what they had said, in the form of a rhetorical question of denial: ﴿And what﴾, i.e., and what thing, ﴿is my knowledge of what they used to do﴾, i.e., before they followed me? That is, what business is it of mine to search into that? For me there is only their present outward state, and it is an excellent outward state (p-65). They are the most honorable, even if they are the poorest of people and the lowliest in lineage, for richness is the richness of religion, and lineage is the lineage of piety.

Then he emphasized, by his saying "in" (إنْ), that he does not investigate their inner states. That is, "their reckoning" (ما حِسابُهُمْ), meaning in the past and the future, "is only upon my Lord" (إلا عَلى رَبِّي), the One who has been good to me by their following me [so that there would be for me the like of their reward], who lightens for me the burden of being charged with their reckoning and with knowing their inner states, because He is the One specifically responsible for recording all deeds and reckoning for them. "If only you perceived" (لَوْ تَشْعُرُونَ), that is: if you had any kind of awareness, you would know this, and you would not have said what you said, which revolves only around worldly affairs, with no regard to the Day of Reckoning.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 114:

When his statement implied something, he rejected what their statement had implied about driving them away, and he made it explicit in his words: ﴿And I am not⁠ ⁠﴾ meaning: "And I am not one who drives away the believers," meaning those for whom faith has become a firmly established attribute, so that they do not turn back from it out of desire for your faith, nor for anything else such as following your desires.

Then he gave the reason for that by his saying: ﴿Not/Nothing﴾, i.e., ﴿I am only a warner﴾, i.e., one who gives warning, not a guardian who calls to account over inward matters, nor one who presses people to follow; ﴿clear﴾, I make clear what I have been sent with, so I leave no ambiguity in it.

When they despaired of driving away his followers, since they had imagined that following him was merely a deception that would cease if he drove them off, they turned to threats. So God, exalted is He, resumed the report of this with His saying: ﴿They said: "If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among those stoned."﴾ Then they addressed him by his name, out of rudeness and lack of courtesy, saying: (p-66) ﴿O Noah, you will surely be among those stoned﴾, i.e., those killed, and your followers, these weak ones, will not benefit you.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 117:

When he despaired of them because of the emphatic exaggeration he heard in their statements, and saw what their deeds confirmed, Allah the Exalted said, reporting about him [as an answer to a question from one who wishes to know his state after that]: ﴿He said﴾, complaining to Allah the Exalted of what He knows better than he does, as a preparation for supplicating against them, an incitement and an arousing towards Him, turning away from their threats to him in patience and seeking reward, because [it is] among the necessary requirements of commanding good and forbidding evil, and as a substitute for it by its cause: ﴿My Lord﴾, meaning: O You who have been good to me.

Since the situation required that they should believe him, because of what he possessed within himself of trustworthiness, and what they had of kinship with him, and since he had established against what he called them to of proofs, along with what he possessed within himself of clarity, he emphasized the report of their denial, informing of its existence and that he had verified it from them without doubt, so he said: ﴿Indeed my people have denied me﴾, meaning: so there is no intention on their part to follow me.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 118:

﴿Fa-iftaḥ﴾ means: judge ﴿between me and them with a judgment (fatḥan)﴾, that is, a judgment through which there will be relief for me, and in which there is an exit from the distress I am in. So destroy the wrongdoers and bring about their doom. ﴿And save me and those with me﴾, that is, in religion, ﴿from the believers﴾, from what You punish the disbelievers with.

(p-67) Since their destruction and his deliverance involved such marvellous craftsmanship as to be beyond description, He presented it in the manifestation of greatness, saying: ﴿So We delivered him and those with him﴾, that is, from those who did not oppose him in religion, despite their weakness and their being killed, ﴿in the ship﴾. And since the safety of something completely filled is more remarkable, He said: ﴿the laden﴾, that is, filled with those carried in it from among people, birds and all kinds of animals, and what was carried of their provisions and whatever would keep them in good condition.

Since the drowning of all of them was among the strange events, he magnified it by using the particle of distance [and the manifestation of greatness], so He said: ﴿Then We drowned the rest afterward﴾, that is, after his carrying (of them) which was the cause of his deliverance, ﴿the rest﴾, that is, those who remained upon the earth and did not board the ship with him, despite their strength and their numbers, [and that was] easy for Us.

[When] that was a manifest matter, he magnified it with His words: ﴿Indeed, in that﴾, i.e., in that great matter of granting respite and then deliverance and destruction, ﴿is surely a sign﴾, i.e., a great sign for whoever witnessed it or heard of it, showing that We take vengeance on those who disobey Us, deliver those who obey Us, and that there is no affair with anyone alongside Us by which He would guide him to faith and bring him to submission and humble acceptance. ﴿And not﴾, i.e., while the reality is that they ﴿were most of them﴾, i.e., most of those who knew of that, ﴿believers﴾. And it was fitting for them, since faith escaped them despite the mere evidence, that they hasten to it and embark with Him when they saw the first signs of the punishment, or after the drowning had gripped them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 122:

﴿And indeed, your Lord﴾ — who shows you kindness by sending you (as a Messenger), by increasing your followers, and by exalting your partisans — ﴿is truly the All-Mighty﴾, i.e., He is able, by His might, to compel each of them to obedience and to destroy them at the very outset of their disobedience, ﴿the Most Merciful﴾, i.e., the One who singles out whomever He wills of His servants with the sincere affection of His love, and who sends Messengers to those who have strayed from the upright path of sound intellect (ʿaql) to explain what He loves and what He dislikes. Thus no one is destroyed except after a clear explanation and a complete delivery of the message.

Since it was as if it were said: "Indeed, this is a dreadful matter, and in its like there is an admonition. So what did those who came after them do? Did they take heed?" he was answered with His saying, indicating both attributes together: ﴿The people of ʿĀd denied the messengers.﴾ That is, that tribe to whom Allah had granted power in the land after the people of Nuh, [denied the messengers] by turning away from the miracle of Hud, peace be upon him;

Then He consoled this noble Prophet ﷺ with His saying: ﴿When﴾ [i.e., at the time when] ﴿their brother Hud said to them﴾, they did not hesitate in denying him, nor did they delay from the time of his call for deliberation or anything else, though they knew his sincerity as a brother, his great counsel and his loyalty. ﴿Will you not﴾, in the form of an offer, out of courtesy toward them, gentleness with them and softness toward them, ﴿fear [Allah]?﴾, i.e., may there come from you taqwa (fear of Allah and God-consciousness) toward your Lord, who created you, so that you worship Him alone and do not associate with Him what neither harms nor benefits.

Then he gave the reason with his saying: ﴿Indeed, I am a messenger to you﴾, i.e., it is this (status) that has compelled me to say that to you. ﴿Trustworthy﴾, i.e., I conceal nothing from you of what I have been commanded with, and I do not oppose any part of it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 126:

﴿So fear Allah﴾, i.e., as a consequence of that, I am telling you: fear ﴿Allah﴾, who is greater than everything, ﴿and obey me﴾, i.e., in everything I command you with, namely continuing to magnify Him. (p-69)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 127:

﴿Wa-ma﴾ (And not), meaning: I am a messenger calling you, and the situation is that I ﴿do not ask you for it﴾, meaning: for the calling, ﴿any reward﴾, so that you might accuse me of it. ﴿In﴾, meaning: ﴿my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 128:

When he (Hud, peace be upon him) had finished calling them to the root, which is faith in the Messenger and the one sent, he followed this with denouncing some of what they were upon, of that which disbelief necessitated, and which occupying oneself with it made necessary, namely persistence in error. He admonished them with [what] had befallen those before them of destruction, as a preface to further emphasis on piety and obedience, because their condition was the condition of those who had forgotten that deluge which destroyed living creatures and demolished buildings. So he said: ﴿Do you build on every high place⌋ a sign (ayah)?﴾ That is, on every elevated place. Abu Hayyan said: Abu 'Ubayda said: the ri'a is the road. Mujahid said: it is the wide path between two mountains. It was said: it is a way, whether or not it has been traversed. Its root in the language is increase,

﴿a sign﴾, that is, a landmark of your strength, because if it were for guidance or something similar, some of the landmarks would suffice rather than all of them.

Since establishing proof of their strength by such means was, upon reflection, of little benefit, he said: ﴿You play the fool.﴾ The intelligent person ought to preserve his precious time (p-70) from frivolity that is not the cause of his salvation, and how could that befit one who has death behind him?

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 129:

Since one who dies should not deny death by deed or word, He said: ﴿And you take for yourselves fortresses (maṣāni')﴾, meaning: things [by drawing water, or lofty palaces and strong fortresses] that you build, which in their solidity are such that they devour time with strength and permanence. None builds them except one whose state is that of one who hopes for eternity. For this reason He said: ﴿so that you may abide forever (takhludūn)﴾, and this is the meaning of what is in al-Bukhari from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him both, of explaining it as "as if you" (ka'annakum).

Since he had made clear that their conduct was the conduct of someone who does not fear death, he followed it with what shows that they do not believe in requital, saying: ﴿And when you seize [anyone]﴾, i.e., [any] one, you seize him with the grip of force in punishment, ﴿you seize like tyrants﴾, i.e., not caring about anything of killing or otherwise. Al-Baghawi said: the jabbar (tyrant) is the one who strikes and kills in anger.

When he had warned them, for this denial, of the punishment of the Overpowering (al-Jabbar), this led him to say: ﴿So fear God﴾, that is, the One to whom belong all the attributes of majesty and generosity, ﴿and obey me﴾.

Since remembering favours obliges submission, he said, encouraging increase and warning against deprivation: ﴿And fear Him who has aided you﴾, i.e., made for you a provision of support (madad), and this is the attaching of a thing to that which strengthens it for orderliness ﴿with what you know﴾, i.e., there is in it no kind of concealment, so that you might be excused for heedlessness regarding restricting it through gratitude.

When he had stated things in summary, he elaborated so that it would be more complete. He said: ﴿He has aided you with livestock﴾, meaning: they help you in your works, and you eat from them and sell them. And when he had mentioned what sustains the bent (of one's livelihood), he followed it with his saying: ﴿and sons﴾, meaning: they help you in what you desire when you are unable (to do it alone).

Then He followed it with what achieves the perfection of living, saying: ﴿And gardens﴾, that is, orchards whose trees are intertwined such that they conceal what is within them. He indicated the continuity of irrigation by His saying: ﴿and springs﴾.

When they were in their aversion, as if they were saying, "What is it that you would keep from us of it?", he said: ﴿Indeed, I fear for you﴾, meaning: because you are my people, what afflicts you grieves me, if you persist in disobedience, ﴿the punishment of a mighty day﴾. And magnifying the day is more emphatic than magnifying the punishment.

﴿They said﴾, content with what they had of the disease of self-admiration, which leads one to find fault with everything that is criticized,

﴿"It is all the same to us whether you admonish﴾, i.e., you warn and caution, and you were the sign of your time in that, by saying of it what no one could match, as indicated by His saying: ﴿or are you not one of those who admonish?﴾, i.e., one qualified for any share of the rank of those firmly grounded in wa'z (admonition), [counted among them, mentioned among them, so it is more eloquent than "or you do not admonish" or "you are not an admonisher"]. Wa'z, as al-Baghawi said, is speech that softens the heart by mentioning promise and threat. The meaning is that the matter is equal in both states, in that we will not obey you in anything. (p-72)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 137:

Then they gave a reason for that by their saying: ﴿This is not﴾, i.e., what ﴿this﴾, i.e., what you have brought us, ﴿is but the custom of the former people﴾ — read with a fatha on the khaʼ and a sukun on the lam in the recitation of Ibn Kathir, Abu ʻAmr and al-Kisa'i (khuluq). ﴿The former people﴾, i.e., their lies; or, what we are in is nothing but the custom of the former people, in the living of some people and the dying of others, and the well-being of one folk and the affliction of others. The recitation of the rest (the remaining readers), with a damma on the khaʼ and the lam, points to this same meaning.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 138:

﴿And we will not be punished.﴾ Because we are a people of strength, courage, valor, and skill.

Having included this denial within what precedes, he made consequent upon it His saying: ﴿So they denied him﴾. Then He made consequent upon it His saying: ﴿So We destroyed them﴾, i.e., by the wind, with the greatness that We possess, before which their greatness is not mentioned, and the strength by which their strength was (established). ﴿Indeed, in that﴾, i.e., in the destruction in every generation of those who disobey and the deliverance of those who obey, ﴿is a sign﴾, i.e., a great sign for those who came after them, indicating that He, glory be to Him, alone does that, because He establishes the truth and nullifies falsehood, and that He does not humiliate those who are with His allies and whoever is with them, and does not exalt those who are against His enemies and whoever is against them. ﴿Yet most of them were not believers﴾, i.e., most of those who came after them. So do not grieve, [O Messenger], over those who turn away from faith.

Verse 140: ﴿And indeed your Lord﴾, i.e., the One who is good to you by sending you and by other blessings, ﴿is the Mighty﴾ in His retribution, ﴿the Merciful﴾ in His bounty, His honoring, and His kindness, despite their disobedience and disbelief, and in sending warners and supporting them with miraculous signs to clarify the most upright path and the safest method. So He does not destroy except after establishing the proof with the most eloquent warning.
Then He indicated this, for one who might forget, since man is created disposed to forgetfulness, by His saying: ﴿Thamud denied the messengers﴾, and they are the people of al-Hijr.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 142:

He indicated the increase of consolation by their confronting him with denial without reflection or pause, through His saying: ﴿When﴾, that is, at the time when ﴿their brother﴾, that is, the one whom they knew to be truthful, trustworthy, compassionate and protective, ﴿Salih said to them﴾. He indicated his gentleness toward them by His saying, in the manner of a suggestion: ﴿Will you not fear God?﴾

Then he gave the reason for that with his saying: ﴿Indeed, I am a messenger to you﴾, that is, from Allah, and therefore I have presented this to you, because I am commanded to do so; otherwise I would not have presented it to you. ﴿Trustworthy﴾: there is nothing of betrayal in me, but rather I give you sincere counsel in conveying everything I have been sent with to you from your Creator, than whom there is no one more merciful to you.

Since he had already mentioned the messengership, and so had an excuse for confronting them with the command, he made his saying the consequence of it: ﴿So fear God﴾, that is, the King, the Most High, who possesses absolute self-sufficiency. And since he had mentioned trustworthiness, he said: ﴿and obey me﴾.

"When he had established what necessitates turning towards him, he negated what entails the habit of turning away from him, so he said: ﴿And I do not ask you for it﴾, i.e., 'I am for you such-and-such, while the state is that I do not ask you for it (any reward)'. He intensified the negation with his saying: ﴿any reward﴾ [then he increased the emphasis of this (p-74) negation with his saying]: ﴿My reward is only﴾, i.e., my reward is not upon anyone except ﴿the Lord of the worlds﴾, i.e., the one who does good to all of them, from Him I seek that He give me as He has given them."

Now that trustworthiness has been established and the cause of betrayal has been removed, he began to rebuke them for consuming his bounty and worshipping other than him. He said, warning them of his assaults and encouraging them toward further of his bounties, rebuking them for their inclining toward the desire of the belly, their reliance on luxury, and their contentment with what is transient: ﴿Will you be left﴾ [i.e., ] from the hands of calamities, which none can control except Allah, ﴿in what is here﴾, i.e., in this land of yours, among these blessings, while you are ﴿secure﴾, i.e., you are challenging the Mighty King with great offenses.

Since explanation after summary (al-tafsir ba'da al-ijmal) has its own importance, he clarified what had been summarized with his words, reminding them of God's blessing so that they might give thanks: ﴿In gardens﴾, that is, orchards that screen whoever enters among them and conceal him because of the abundance of their trees, ﴿and springs﴾ that water them, along with the delight they possess and other benefits.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 148:

﴿And fields of crops﴾. He points to the great importance of palm trees, especially among them, by singling them out for mention after their inclusion in the gardens, with His words: ﴿and palm trees whose spathes are tender﴾, meaning what emerges from them of fruit. Al-Zamakhshari said: "Like the blade of a sword within its sheath are the shamarikh (spikelets) of the qinw (bunch of dates). The qinw is the name for what emerges from the trunk, as is its 'arjun (stalk) and its shamarikh."

﴿Hadim﴾ means generous and bountiful, from the saying of the Arabs: "a hadum hand," when it gives freely of what it has. Explaining it this way brings together the sayings of the scholars. To it returns what Abu 'Abd Allah al-Qazzaz (p-75) said of its meaning: that it has been hadama (compressed), meaning some of it has been pressed by others because of its abundance, for it is not like this unless it is plentiful, closely packed together, with no gaps between it. It is also delicate, soft, brittle and good-smelling, from al-hadam (with vowel movement), which is the thinness of the belly and slenderness of the waist. Al-hadim is that which has softness in it. Al-hadm is incense, and al-mahdumah is a perfume mixed with musk and frankincense. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': "Or it is ripe, ready, soft and loose, and crumbles and breaks apart when touched, or it digests food." All of this returns to its delicacy.

When he had mentioned the refined aspects of their circumstances, he followed it with the coarse aspects of their deeds, saying, by way of conjunction with ﴿Will you be left...﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 26:146], or as an explanation of the state of the agent in ﴿secure﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 26:146]: ﴿and you hew﴾, meaning, while you are hewing, to display power, ﴿out of the mountains, houses, exultant﴾, meaning, displaying vigor and strength, boasting and exulting in that, not because you need anything of that.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 150:

﴿So fear God﴾, i.e., as a consequence of that, I say to you: fear ﴿God﴾, to whom belongs all greatness, by making between yourselves and His punishment a shield, through following His commands and avoiding His prohibitions. ﴿And obey me﴾, i.e., in everything I command you and forbid you from, for I only command you with what sets your affairs right, so that it becomes a cause for preserving what you are in and for your increase.

﴿And do not obey﴾ (p. 76). Since submission to the one who commands comes only through what has become evident of his command, He said: ﴿the command of the extravagant﴾, that is, those who transgress the limits, for whom this has become a settled disposition (khuluq);.

Then He described them with what makes their extravagance clear, namely committing pure, unmixed corruption in which there is no good at all, and so He said: ﴿who spread corruption in the land﴾, meaning: they do what leads to corruption, because it is not firmly founded on its reliance upon Allah.

And since it might be claimed that some corruption contains some good, He negated that with His saying: ﴿and do not reform﴾, meaning: because they founded their affair upon polytheism (shirk), they reached a state in which no work is sound for them, even if it appears otherwise. Or the meaning is that the extravagant one is he who is deeply rooted in extravagance by combining these two matters.

Since he called to God, Exalted is He, with what has no flaw in it, and they knew they were unable to find fault in any part of it, they turned to imagination, playing on the minds of the weak, by saying: ﴿You are only one of the bewitched﴾. That is, those who have been subjected to sorcery again and again, while being human beings with a sahr (sahr: the lungs, the windpipe region), so that the magic has affected you until it has overcome you. Al-Baghawi transmits from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that its meaning is: among the created beings who are sustained by food and drink. It is said: "saharahu," meaning he sustained him with food and drink. This interpretation is supported by their explanation with the phrase that indicates he is not fit for prophethood.

(p-77) ﴿You are only a human being like us.﴾ That is: what is the basis for your being singled out from us with prophethood? Can a Messenger be one of the humans? Their following the description with the description, without a conjunction between them, indicates that they were not firm in denying him. For them the two descriptions are like a single thing, as when it is said: "The pomegranate is sweet, sour," meaning mazz (bitter-tasting). What confirms that they were at the level of doubt, and did not go beyond it to certainty or even to the supposition of denial, is their saying: ﴿Then bring us a sign﴾, that is, a sign that shows us your truthfulness, ﴿if you are﴾, that is, in a state that is firmly established, ﴿among the truthful﴾, that is, those deeply rooted in truthfulness. This is unlike what comes soon in the story of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 155:

When God swiftly answered his supplication, when he prayed that they be given what they had proposed, He indicated this by His saying: ﴿He said﴾, that is, in reply to their proposal: "Come, look at what I bring you as a sign of my truthfulness." So they came, and God brought forth for him from the rock a she-camel heavy with young (ʿushshar), just as they had proposed. Then, pointing to her with the particle of proximity, indicating the ease and speed of her bringing forth, he said: ﴿This is a she-camel﴾, that is, my Lord brought her forth from the rock just as you proposed. Then he indicated that in this sign there is another sign, namely that she drinks all the water of the well on her day of watering and refrains from it on the second day, for their sake, by His saying: ﴿She shall have a share of drink﴾, that is, a portion of the water on a known day, ﴿and you shall have a share of drink, a known day﴾, that is, a portion of the water on a ﴿known﴾ day, with no crowding between you and her in anything of that.

When the context had clearly guided to the meaning, "So take your drink and leave her drink to her," he followed it with His saying: ﴿And do not touch her with harm﴾, i.e., whatever it may be and however small, because what comes from Allah must be honored, cared for and respected. Then he warned them with what results from their disobedience, saying: ﴿Lest there seize you﴾, i.e., destroy you, ﴿the punishment of a great Day﴾, because of what befell therein of punishment. This is more eloquent than describing the punishment as great.

He indicated the swiftness of their disobedience by the fa' of sequence in His saying: ﴿So they hamstrung her﴾ [i.e., they killed her by striking her leg with the sword].

When the hamstringing of her caused the signs of punishment to descend, He reported their regret over killing her from the standpoint that it would lead to destruction, not from the standpoint that it was an act of disobedience to Allah and His Messenger. So He said: ﴿Then they became regretful﴾, i.e., over hamstringing her, because the punishment had become certain.

Alternatively, it points out that this regret was not in the form of repentance, or that it was at the sight of the punishment, so it did not benefit them; or that this is a metaphor for the fact that their state became the state of one who regrets, not that some regret was actually found among them of any sort. For it has been transmitted from them that the punishment came upon them while they were trying to kill Salih, peace be upon him, by his saying: ﴿So the punishment seized them﴾, meaning: the punishment with which they had been threatened.

And since the she-camel and the appearance of the signs, as has been mentioned previously, were the greatest proof of the truthfulness of the Messenger who called to Allah, He said: ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign﴾, meaning: a great indication of the correctness of what they were commanded with from Allah,

﴿and yet﴾, meaning: while the state is that, despite all that, ﴿most of them were not believers﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 159:

Since it might be imagined that He, glory be to Him, is not characterized by might (ʿizza) because He does not compel them to belief, or by mercy (raḥma) because He destroys them, He said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is truly the Mighty﴾, that is, nothing escapes His grip and His will, and He is the One who willed for them disbelief; ﴿the Merciful﴾ in that He did not destroy anyone until He sent to them a messenger who made clear to them what He, glory be to Him, is pleased with and what angers Him, and who gave them thorough warning until He established the proof by that. Then He, glory be to Him, misguides whom He wills, because of what He knows of their nature regarding that which entails wretchedness, and guides whomever He knows to have good in him to what pleases Him, so that his happiness results from that. In His, glory be to Him, repeating this verse at the end of every story, for emphasis, and in following it with what it indicates of the disbelief of those who came after its people, without taking warning from their condition or refraining from the like of their error out of fear of the like of their punishment, is the greatest consolation for this noble Prophet, and a warning for every knowing, forbearing person, and an appeal to every person of sound heart. For this reason (p-80) He said, connecting to the story:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 160:

﴿Kadhdhabat﴾ meaning: the custom of those who came before them, as if they had agreed upon it together. ﴿The people of Lut denied the messengers﴾. Because whoever denies one messenger, as has passed, has denied all of them, due to the equality of the miracles in indicating truthfulness. This verse has explicitly stated their disbelief through denial, and it clarifies their haste in going astray by His saying.
