For this reason, he made his following statement a consequence of it.

﴿So fear Allah﴾ [meaning]: due to His power to destroy whomever He wills, and His exaltedness in His greatness. ﴿And obey me﴾ meaning: because my obedience is the cause of your salvation, for I only command you with what He is pleased with, and I only forbid you from what angers Him.

(p-81) When he had established the one who calls to obedience to Him (the messenger), he negated the one who forbids it, saying: ﴿And I ask of you no wage for it﴾, i.e., for the calling to Allah, ﴿any wage﴾, i.e., lest you accuse me on account of it. He also negated seeking anything from the rest of creation by specifying it to the Creator, saying: ﴿My wage is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾, i.e., the One who bestows favor upon them by bringing them into existence and then nurturing them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 165:

When they found the impetus to follow it [i.e., to follow the desire] and the obstacle was removed, he [Allah] denounced them for what necessitates their punishment [namely, their preference for the lust of the private parts, which brought them to a state where they became a disgrace among creation]. So He said, rebuking and reproaching them, to make clear how monstrous and grave their act was: ﴿Do you approach the males﴾ [i.e., approach them in sin], ﴿of the worlds?﴾ Perhaps they used to do this with males from among non-human beings, going to extremes in evil and openly flaunting their depravity, given His words: ﴿of the worlds﴾, i.e., all of them. Or the meaning is: among all creatures, i.e., you have singled yourselves out for approaching males; none of the other creatures [among those who engage in intercourse] has done this act.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 166:

﴿And leave﴾ i.e., you abandon for this purpose ﴿what your Lord has created for you﴾ i.e., marriage (nikah), ﴿your Lord﴾, the One who is good to you, ﴿of your spouses﴾ i.e., and they are the females, on the basis that "min" (ﻣِﻦ, "of") is for explanation (bayan). It is also permissible for it to be partitive (tab'id), and the created thing would then be, in that manner, the front passage (al-qubul).

And since they were as if they had said: "We have not abandoned our spouses," interpreting his words as abandonment in its root and entirety, even though they understood that his intent was abandoning them during the act with males, he (God) turned away from their statement, which was known, its estimation being what they intended by it, swerving from the truth and persisting in wickedness, saying: ﴿Nay, but you are a people who transgress﴾ i.e., you have abandoned the spouses by extending the act to them and going beyond it to the act with males. That is no novelty from your affair, for transgression (al-'udwan), which is exceeding the limit in evil, is a description of you, in which you are deeply rooted; therefore you do not stop at any limit that God Most High has set.

فَلَمّا اتَّضَحَ الحَقُّ، وعُرِفَ المُرادُ، وكانَ غَرِيبًا عِنْدَهم، وتَشَوَّفَ السّامِعُ إلى جَوابِهِمْ، اسْتُؤْنِفَ الإخْبارُ عَنْهُ، فَقِيلَ إعْلامًا بِانْقِطاعِهِمْ وأنَّهم عارِفُونَ أنَّهُ لا وجْهَ لَهم في ذَلِكَ أصْلًا لِعُدُولِهِمْ إلى الفُحْشِ: ﴿قالُوا﴾ مُقْسِمِينَ: ﴿لَئِنْ لَمْ تَنْتَهِ﴾ [وسَمَّوْهُ بِاسْمِهِ جَفاءً وغِلْظَةً فَقالُوا: ] ﴿يا لُوطُ﴾ عَنْ مَثَلِ إنْكارِكَ هَذا عَلَيْنا.

Then, since the greatness of what he had through prophethood and noble deeds, which obliges their reverence and the denial that anyone who hears them should go out like him, was evident, they increased the emphasis and said: ﴿لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ المُخْرَجِينَ﴾ meaning: [among those] whom we expel from our town [in a hideous manner by which you become known among them], indicating that he is a stranger among them, and that their constant custom is to expel whoever objects to them. Their intention in this was that they themselves would be the ones to expel him, as humiliation to him and to relieve themselves of him. So his expulsion happened, but it was an expulsion of honour, for relief from them and for deliverance from their punishment through the noble angels taking charge of it. (p-٨٣)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 168:

﴿Qāla﴾ (He said), i.e., in answer to them. ﴿Innī﴾ (Indeed I), emphasizing the content of what follows, ﴿li-ʿamalikum﴾ (of your deed). He did not say "qāla" alone; rather he added to the emphasis with his words: ﴿min al-qālīn﴾ (among those who detest it), i.e., those well known for hating this vile deed, deeply rooted in this quality, and famed among people for shunning whoever commits it. Your threat to expel me, or anything else, will not turn me back from denouncing it. Al-qilāʾ (detestation) is intense hatred, as if it scorches the heart (yaqlī al-fu'ād).

When He had begun with the like of this, which by its nature leads to evil, He turned to the One who does such things for their sake, and He is the One capable of all things, the One who knows all things, and so He said: ﴿My Lord, deliver me and my family from what﴾, that is, from the punishment that will overtake them, ﴿because of what they do﴾.

When Allah, glorified and exalted is He, accepted his supplication, He indicated this by His saying: ﴿So We saved him and his family﴾ from what We had punished them with, by Our bringing him out of their land when they treated him with contempt. He did not delay him from them until the time of his departure except for his sake. Allah, glorified is He, specified the intended meaning, making clear that his family was numerous, by His saying: ﴿all together﴾, that is, the people of his household and those who followed him in his religion.

﴿Except an old woman﴾, who was his wife, being ﴿among﴾ those who remain behind, i.e., those who stay (al-ghabirin), upon whom the dust (al-ghabarah) of the calamity that befalls them settles. We did not deliver her, because We had decreed that in eternity, since she did not follow him in the religion, and her inclination was with her people.

(p. 84) When he mentioned their deliverance, which implied their destruction, he stated the destruction explicitly in a way that conveys its awfulness, using the particle of delay (thumma) because it is known, as has been noted more than once, that it occurred immediately after his departure, with no interval between them. So He said: ﴿Then We destroyed the others﴾, i.e., We destroyed them with a sudden destruction [a stern, deaf (unyielding) one, in the utmost of misfortune]. How excellent is the expression of referring to them with the word ﴿the others﴾, to convey that their coming later was in every respect.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 173:

Since the meaning of ﴿dammarna﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 172] is "We decreed their destruction," He joined to it His saying: ﴿wa-amtarna﴾ ("and We rained"). He indicated the punishment by its construction with "ʿalā" (upon), saying: ﴿ʿalayhim maṭaran﴾ ("upon them a rain"), meaning: and what a rain it was! For this reason, He made the following a consequence of it: ﴿fa-sāʾa maṭaru l-mundharīn﴾ ("so evil was the rain of those who had been warned"), meaning: how evil was the rain of those whom Lot, peace be upon him, warned, by what his denunciation and his expression of taqwa (God-consciousness) and 'udwan (transgression) pointed to.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 174:

Since the passing of the deniers and the affirmers, under one system of destruction and salvation, is the greatest lesson and the most mighty admonition, he pointed to that with His saying: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign﴾, that is: a great proof of the truthfulness of the Messengers in all of their encouraging and warning, their giving good news and their giving warning.

And since those who came after these nations, such as the Quraysh and those before them, have known their reports, and have joined to some of the reports the viewing of the dwellings and the discerning of the traces (p-85), He said, marveling at their state in their misguidance: ﴿And not ﴾, that is: while the state is that ﴿most of them were believers﴾.

When the previous verses contained an indication of warning with the like of the destruction that befell them, he followed it with an explicit statement of both fear and hope, saying: ﴿And indeed your Lord — He is⦌ — that is, He alone — ﴿the Almighty﴾ [i.e., ] in His seizing of His enemies, ﴿the Most Merciful﴾ in His gentleness toward His friends, and His kindness toward His enemies by sending the Messengers and clarifying every difficulty;

Then he joined to this its proof, and said, mentioning the verb (in the masculine form, kadhdhaba) because of the intensity of their disbelief, as evidenced by the presence of the waw (in the later verse) in ﴿وما أنْتَ إلا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُنا﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 186] ("You are but a mortal like us"). ﴿The companions of the Thicket (al-Aykah) denied the messengers﴾. That is: the thicket (al-ghay∂ah), the place of good land which swallows up water and so produces abundant, densely intertwined trees. ﴿The messengers﴾: because of their denial of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) regarding what he brought of the heavenly miracle—in breaking of the customary order, and the inability of those who challenged him with it to withstand it—along with the remaining miracles that the prophets, may prayers and peace be upon them all, brought.

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿When Shu'ayb said to them﴾.

Since they were people of the desert (badw) and he, peace be upon him, was from a town (qarawi), he said: ﴿Shu'ayb﴾ [and did not say "their brother," indicating] that he did not send any prophet except from among the people of towns, honouring them, because blessing and wisdom lie in gathering together. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade becoming a Bedouin (ta'arrub) after the Hijrah, and said: "Whoever God desires good for, He will move him from the desert to the town." ﴿Will you not fear God?﴾ That is: you would become among the people of taqwa (God-consciousness), and it is fear of God, glorified and exalted is He.

Since it was as if it were said, "What is your concern with this?", he said: ﴿Indeed I﴾, and he pointed to their good tidings if they obeyed him with his saying: ﴿a messenger to you﴾, i.e., from God; so He commanded me to say that to you. ﴿Trustworthy﴾, i.e., there is no deceit (ghishsh) with me, nor deception (khida'), nor betrayal (khiyana). Therefore I convey everything I have been sent with, and for this reason he made his saying the consequence of that.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 179:**

﴿So fear Allah﴾, i.e., the One who deserves all greatness, and who has been good to you with this thicket and others besides it. ﴿And obey me﴾ [i.e.,] because of what has been established of my sincere counsel.

Having placed first what is the primary object (of the discourse), he joined to the predicate of "inna" the statement: ﴿And I do not ask you for any wage for it﴾, negating what would repel (the listeners) from it. Then he added to the disavowal of what diminishes (one's) longing for any of creation, and said: ﴿Verily﴾, that is: ﴿my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾, [that is:] the One who is good to all creatures. So I never hope from anyone who needs to be benefited by me; rather I hang my hope on the Benefactor who needs no one, while every person is a seeker of His bounty and a taker from His presence. It has become clear that the Messengers agree in the call: in commanding taqwa (God-consciousness) and obedience, sincerity in worship, along with counsel, chastity, trustworthiness, awe (of God), and love (of Him).

Since it is as though it had been said, "What is it that you are warning them about?", he said, [clarifying that their disease was love of wealth, which leads them to a bad state,] ﴿Give full measure﴾, that is: complete it, completing it without any doubt, when you measure, as you complete it when you take measure for yourselves. When he commanded them to give full measure, he forbade them from shortfall in a more general way, saying: ﴿and do not be among those who cause loss﴾, that is, a state that is like a natural disposition. Perhaps this is an allusion to such things as occur from thoughts or states in which human nature overcomes a person, and then he returns from them with a return that erases them. For this reason he said: ﴿among the losers﴾, that is, those who suffer loss, meaning those who diminish themselves, their religion, by diminishing the people's worldly goods through short measure or other kinds of shortfall, from every matter that brings about deception. Thus you would be known for that among those who practice it.

When He commanded the full measure, He followed it with the like of it in weighing, and He did not join the two together, because separating them conveys a greater emphasis on the matter. So He said: ﴿Weigh with a true balance﴾, that is, for yourselves and for others, ﴿with the balance (al-qistas)﴾, that is, the most upright scale; and He reinforced its meaning with His words: ﴿the straight﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 183:

When He had commanded fulfilling the measure in weighing, He followed it with a general prohibition against neglecting it, as He had done with measuring [so that it would be more emphatic], saying: ﴿And do not diminish for people their things﴾, i.e., do not deprive them, ﴿their things﴾ (p-88), i.e., in measuring, or weighing, or other than these, by a deficiency that is like a salt-marsh (sabkha), having no benefit in it. Then He followed that with something more general than it, saying: ﴿And do not go about in the earth﴾, i.e., do not act, ﴿in the earth﴾ without deliberation, while you are ﴿causing corruption﴾, i.e., in wealth or otherwise, intending by that corruption, as its explanation has preceded in Surat Hud, peace be upon him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 184:

When he had admonished them and made his admonition effective by concluding it with the prohibition of corruption (fasad), he warned them of the seizures (satawat) of God, the Exalted, by what He brought down upon those greater than them. So He said: ﴿And fear Him who created you﴾, meaning: their annihilation is the easiest thing for Him. He indicated their weakness and the strength of those who came before them by His saying: ﴿and the former generations (al-jibilla)﴾, meaning: the community and the nation ﴿of old﴾, who were of a great constitution and nature, as if they were mountains in strength and firmness, especially the people of Hud, peace be upon him, who were Arabs like you, and whose intensity in their bodies and firmness in all their limbs reached the point that they said ﴿Who is mightier than us in strength?﴾ [Fussilat: 15]. And what He, glorified is He, sent down upon them of His might has reached you, because the Arabs are the people most knowledgeable of their histories.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 185:

When what had been achieved so far was the announcement of the messengership and the warning against opposing it, because that leads to misguidance, he concluded that with an allusion, by expressing with the word "creation" (al-jibillah) that His punishment, exalted is He, is great, and nothing small or great can resist Him. They answered him by discrediting the messengership first, and by belittling the threat second, saying ﴿You are only one of the bewitched﴾. That is: those whose magic was repeated time after time until they became deranged, so their speech came out without order; or one of those who are sustained with food and drink, as passed in the case of Salih, peace be upon him. That is: you are far from being fit for messengership.

Then they pointed to the impossibility, in any absolute sense, of humans being able to do this, even if they were the most intelligent of people and the furthest from calamity, by their saying, connecting with "and" (waw) to indicate its deep-rootedness in what they described him with, namely sorcery and being bewitched, and that there is no difference between him and them: ﴿You are only a human like us﴾ [i.e.,] so there is no basis for singling you out from us with this. The evidence that this conjunction (ʿaṭf) is more emphatic than following it without conjunction is their certainty about his being a liar in their saying: ﴿And indeed﴾ i.e., and indeed we ﴿think you are among the liars﴾ i.e., among the most profoundly entrenched in lying. This is the position of the Basrans that "in" (inna) is a lightened form of the heavy one (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla). What the context requires here is the preference for the position of the Kufans that "in" is a negation particle, for they intended, by affirming the waw [in] ﴿and [what]﴾, emphasis in negating his being sent, by multiplying the "mā" that negates it. So their meaning is that we have no supposition that goes in any direction other than lying, and this is more emphatic than affirming supposition about him. It is supported by (p-90) their making his request for the punishment's descent a consequence of it, mocking him and challenging him, unlike what preceded regarding the people of Ṣāliḥ, peace be upon him. So they said.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 187:**

﴿Then cause fragments of the sky to fall upon us﴾ — read with the sukun on the sin (ﺱ) according to the common reading (qira'at al-jama'ah), and with a fatha on it in the transmission of Hafs. Both are the plural of kisfah, meaning pieces, ﴿from the sky﴾, that is, clouds, or the literal sky. This demand comes from their determination to deny, and had there been in them the slightest inclination toward belief, they would not have entertained it in their minds [let alone asked for it, especially since it was in a mocking manner; for this reason they said]: ﴿if you are﴾, that is, of a nature that is as a natural disposition for you, ﴿among the truthful﴾, that is, those who are firmly established in truthfulness and well known among their people, [so that we would believe you] regarding what is incumbent upon us from your command to take precautions against the punishment, from the threat of punishment. How excellent is his observation of their threat, with what God has over them of power in creating them and creating those who were stronger than them, and in destroying them with various kinds of punishment when they disobeyed Him by denying His messengers.

Since the punishment of the disobedient depends on knowledge that encompasses their deeds and power to inflict retribution, God, exalted is He, resumed relating his words in admonishing them about this, by saying: ﴿He said﴾, indicating that none of that belongs to anyone except the One who sent him, who is characterized by both attributes. As for himself, although he has knowledge, his knowledge is limited, and he is not capable (of punishing). ﴿My Lord knows best﴾, that is, better than me, ﴿what you do﴾, because He has all-encompassing knowledge and all-comprehensive power. He knows your deserving of punishment, the measure of what you deserve from it, and the time of its descent. So if He wills, He will punish you. As for me, there is nothing upon me except conveying the message, and I am commanded to do so. I did not threaten you with myself, nor did I claim power to punish you; therefore your demand of that from me is an injustice on your part, added to your injustice of denial.

Al-Biqa'i's commentary (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 189:

Since the whole aim of their speech was their denial of him, without any disparagement of the power of the Creator, He linked the punishment to their denial, saying: ﴿So they denied him﴾, meaning they persisted in denying him. ﴿Then the punishment of the Day of the Shade seized them﴾, meaning a seizing of destruction. The "Day of the Shade" (yawm al-zullah) was a cloud, in the manner of what they had asked for, namely pieces of the sky falling. It came upon them after a severe heat that had afflicted them, even in the caverns within the earth, more intensely than the heat they had suffered outside, so that it might be known that there is no doer but Allah, and that He disposes things as He wills, both according to the customary course and beyond it. They found from that shade a cool breeze and a pleasant air, so they gathered beneath it, seeking refreshment and shelter in it. Then it rained down fire upon them, and they were burned in a manner similar to what they had proposed. Allah came to them from where they did not reckon, so the arrows of His power penetrated among them, and they found no protection or shelter from anything beyond it, without any need for a piece of the body of the sky to fall, nor for anything beneath it from the clouds.

Since the situation calls for a question about the Day of the Shade, the Exalted said, magnifying its matter and exalting its rank: ﴿Indeed, it was﴾, He emphasized with "inna" [and magnified with "kana"] ﴿a punishment of a tremendous day﴾, and He increased its greatness by attributing it to the day, so that it acquired, through the wondrous nature of this statement, a terror that makes hearts tremble and calamities grow great.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 190:

Since the successive reports of the destruction of these generations, and the annihilation of those nations mentioned, produce a terror whose description cannot be reached and whose explanation is not possible for anyone other than Him, glory be to Him, He said, pointing to it as a warning against the like of it: ﴿Indeed, in that⁠﻿ is a sign⁠﻿ — that is, in the great matter of the continual deliverance of every messenger and those who obeyed him, and the continual seizing of those who disobeyed him in every age and in every land, such that not one person from either group, near or far, is left out — ﴿a sign﴾, that is, a clear and great proof of the truthfulness of the messengers, and that they are worthy of the servants believing them in all that they said of glad tidings and warnings: that God Most High destroys whoever disobeys Him and saves whoever is loyal to Him, because He is the free, chosen Doer, with no one to prevent Him. This is especially so for you, and you are the greatest of them in station and the most honored of them in rank. It is especially so since you brought your people that which would leave no room for doubt even if they had no prior knowledge of you; how much more so when they know that before the prophethood you were the most truthful of them in speech, the greatest of them in trustworthiness, the most abundant of them in intellect, the clearest of them in nobility, the highest of them in aspiration, and the furthest of them from every stain, however slight its trace. Then He expressed wonder at their hesitation in believing, despite what they knew of the truthfulness of their Prophet, the purity of his character, and the abundance of his compassion toward them, and that they did not fear the like of what they had verified of the destruction of these nations. So He said: ﴿And most of them were not believers﴾, that is, most of your people, as was the case with those before them, despite seeing these signs and the descent of these punishments, to the point that it is as though they had made a pact together on this. ﴿Believers﴾, that is, firmly established in faith. Rather, they do not believe except that they are polytheists.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 191:

When all of this was a consolation for the caller (to the faith) ﷺ, a threat to whoever persisted in denying him, and a source of hope for whoever turned back from his sins, he indicated this by His saying: ﴿And indeed your Lord﴾, i.e., the One who is good to you in everything that elevates your station and clarifies your proof, ﴿is truly the Almighty﴾, so no one can overpower Him, and His granting respite to a disobedient person is not attributed to neglect or incapacity, ﴿the Most Merciful﴾, so He does not seize except after the limit has been exceeded and there is no hope of a response, together with a clear explanation, a complete delivery of the message, and sufficient gentleness. He repeated this closing statement in this surah eight times. Perhaps among its secrets is an indication of the precedence of mercy over wrath, because the surah that opened with the Upright Book (al-Kitab al-Qayyim) and the Perfect Servant, in relation to the Greatest King, which are the mercy of the Creator to the creatures, and which mentioned in it [despite placing it first in the context of warning] the people of mercy from the People of the Cave (p-94) who said ﴿Grant us mercy from Yourself﴾ [Al 'Imran: 8] [and Musa and al-Khidr, peace be upon them both, to each of whom He gave mercy from Himself], and Dhul-Qarnayn, to whom He gave a means to everything, so he followed a means, and he said: ﴿This is a mercy from my Lord﴾ [al-Kahf: 98] — up to the surah of mercy, through the sending down of the Criterion (al-Furqan) upon His servant to whom He is attributed, as a warning that announces the attribute of might — eight surahs, so each of the two is the eighth of the other. The surah that follows, the one concerned with the Criterion, opened with a detailed explanation of what is at the beginning of al-Kahf, through His saying: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 3], and through the mention of what is on the earth of adornment: ﴿Have they not seen the earth, how many noble pairs of every kind We have caused to grow in it?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 7]. All of this was a reminder of what is in that Book, which gathers mercy, and a warning against what is in the Qur'an of the distinguishing warning of might. When that was so, the two attributes of might, which the Criterion announced, and mercy, which the Cave made explicit, were repeated eight times according to that number, as a reminder of this wondrous meaning, and as encouragement, intimidation, and reminder of the eight gates of mercy, together with the awe that the closing of the stories with this brings to the soul, the dread in the heart, and the profound intimacy for the spirit. [Here the attribute of might was placed first, looking to the warning by the Criterion, in the manner of a scattered arrangement, together with what that requires of the state here.] The stories were made seven as a warning against the seven gates of vengeance, along with other secrets that thought cannot contain.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 192:

[p-95] When the traces of these stories were visible signs, and the reports of them were audible signs, and in the consistent destruction of the disobedient and deliverance of the obedient in each of them, despite the distance of eras, the remoteness of regions, and the variety of lands, [there is] the greatest proof of the truthfulness of the messengers, and confirmation of the messages, because of their agreement in calling to God and their converging on monotheism and justice, together with their abstention from this world, which is pure evil, and their turning to the Hereafter, which is pure good, and their adornment with what the servants have unanimously agreed to be the lofty qualities of character and the good deeds, and their clearing of all base things and their purity from every deficiency, He joined to His saying at the beginning of the surah ﴿And there does not come to them any reminder...﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 5] the verse, the report of the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ), as an indication of what there is in the reporting of the traces of these stories as audible signs of great indications of his mission (ﷺ), by what they contain of inimitability in terms of composition and arrangement and other wondrous styles, which [no] nation of the bygone nations was given; and in terms of the fact that the one who brings these strange stories and wondrous, marvellous reports is an unlettered man who did not mix with any scholar [together with the strong suitability of the Qur'an to the specific content of the story of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, concerning justice in measure and weight, which is the pivot of the Qur'an, and that it is the all-encompassing shade of good, and the tent that repels every harm]; so He said, as a response from the conclusion to the opening: ﴿And indeed it is﴾, i.e., the Reminder [p-96] which brought them these reports while they turn away from it and abandon it, ﴿a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾, i.e., the One who nurtured them with the comprehensiveness of His knowledge and the greatness of His power, with what none other can do even in the least of it, because He brought them the truth of these matters through the tongue of one who never mixed with any scholar at all; and although He, glorified is He, nourished them with His bounty and managed them with His wisdom, His wisdom required that this Reminder be comprehensive by being the seal, and that it be inimitable by being complete, and He sent it down gradually, bit by bit, repeating within it the mention of the stories mentioned earlier, in each surah what suits the purpose of that surah, expressing what it presents of them in a manner that fits the aim of that context, while observing reality and conformity with what exists.

The situation called for someone to ask: who brought this speech, from the Possessor of Majesty? So He said: ﴿Brought down by it﴾, meaning in installments, by way of gradual revelation, from the highest horizon, which is the place of blessings. He expressed Jibril, peace be upon him, by the words ﴿the Spirit﴾, indicating that he is a source of goodness, and that the spirits come with what he brings down of guidance. And He said ﴿the Trustworthy﴾, pointing to the fact that he is protected from every impurity, so that betrayal is not possible from him.

﴿Upon your heart﴾, meaning: O Muhammad, the heart that is the noblest and highest of hearts, the most precise and the most retentive, so that there is no deviation in it and no crookedness, (p-97) until it became his character. Omitting the intermediary (wāsiṭa) indicates that, because of the intensity of his giving ear and the presence of his senses (ḥiss), he becomes so firmly established in it that he preserves it and does not forget it, and understands it in its true understanding and it is not hidden from him. Thus its entry into the heart is extremely easy, as if it reached the heart without the mediation of hearing, the opposite of what is related about the criminals. Likewise, everyone who takes in something with the utmost attentiveness preserves it entirely. Consider His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you, and say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge﴾ [Ta-Ha: 114], and ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 16], and the verse.

Since the context of this surah is one of warning, he said, giving the reason for the clause before it: ﴿so that you may be among the warners﴾, meaning: those who frighten and warn those who turn away from faith and commit what He has forbidden of disobedience.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 195:

Since the purpose of the surah is consolation regarding their non-belief, [the reason being] that their own standing had become base, not any defect in its exposition or any deficiency in its status, Allah the Exalted said [clarifying its firm establishment before him]: ﴿in the clear Arabic tongue﴾. And since there is in Arabic what is uncouth in wording or structure, difficult for many Arabs, He said: ﴿clear﴾, meaning: clear in itself, revealing what is intended by it, leaving no ambiguity for whoever reflects upon it (p-98) with due reflection, according to what the Arabs customarily use in their address, from all their languages, with its literal and metaphorical senses, given the breadth of its meanings, the remoteness of its aims in their discourse, and the excellence of its intentions in their metonymies and metaphors. None encompasses all of that with full comprehensiveness except the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, the All-Aware, the All-Seeing. Its Arabic character and its clarity were only to make it plain that it preceded his heart, because whoever speaks in a language, how much more so in its clearest forms, the meanings precede the words to his heart. Had he been a non-Arab, it would have descended upon his hearing only, for he would hear the jingling of letters without understanding their meanings. Al-Kashshaf says: A man may know several languages, and when he is addressed in the language in which he was first taught, grew up, and was formed, his heart goes only to the meanings and he hardly notices the words; but if he is addressed in another language, even if he is skilled in it, his attention first goes to its words and then to their meanings. End of quote. In this there is a great rebuke for whoever knows the tongue of the Arabs yet does not believe in it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 196:

Since accumulating evidence is among the things that calm souls and bring hearts to rest, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And indeed, it﴾, that is, this Qur'an, its fundamental principles, many of its narratives, and the foundational mother-branches of its rulings, ﴿is in the scriptures of the former peoples﴾, that is, the books of ﴿the earlier ones﴾, which are preserved and well known for having come down from heaven to their peoples, whose souls were at ease in the knowledge that messengers had come to them, and that laws had been prescribed for them, and that books had been revealed to them with these laws, without this which was brought by him (ﷺ) having been mixed with anyone among them or among others in any knowledge whatsoever. This was a decisive proof that it was brought to him by none other than Allah the Exalted.

When the implied sense was: "Was it not a sign for them of the truth of this that they should seek those scriptures, examine them, and thereby taste it, so that they might be led to the certainty of truth?", he followed it with His saying: ﴿Is it not a sign for them﴾.

[Since this style is one of inference, the majority reading, with the masculine form and the accusative, required placing the predicate before the subject. So after putting forward what the context required, he said:] ﴿a sign﴾, meaning: a token of its ascription to Us. Then he followed that noun with a clause introduced by *an* (that) and a verb, transformed from it, because this is more specific, more definite, and clearer than mentioning the verbal noun. So he said: ﴿that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it﴾, meaning: that what our Prophet brought is from Us. Ibn 'Amir read the verb in the feminine and made ﴿sign﴾ the subject in the nominative, predicating it with *an* and the verb: ﴿that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it﴾, [so that they would acknowledge it] and would not deny it, in order that they would believe in it and not abandon it. For the Quraysh would often refer to them and rely on them regarding divine reports. Many of them embraced Islam, and they mentioned that the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms and the other books of the prophets, peace be upon them, confirm the Qur'an concerning the description of the Prophet ﷺ. In that there is what supports his truthfulness and establishes his matter. The books mentioned were later translated into Arabic, and the Muslim scholars extracted from them much [of what] they had neglected, as proof against them. There is no difference in this between those among them who embraced Islam and others, for at the time the Qur'an was revealed, alteration had already occurred in them, as God Most High informed us. [And] it is related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that the people of Makkah sent envoys to the Jews to ask them about Muhammad ﷺ. They said: "This is his time, and we find his description in the Torah." That was binding upon them by the report of God Most High. Likewise, whatever is extracted from the books will be a proof against their people.

The commentary is on surah 26, verse 198. Its phrase "ولَمّا كانَ التَّقْدِيرُ" is rendered below with the Qur'anic quotations kept in the required markers.

When the sense (taqdir) was: "They did not see in any of that a sign, nor did they believe," he conjoined to it, or to His words, may He be exalted, at the beginning of the surah: ﴿So they have denied﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 6], the verse: ﴿And if We had sent it down﴾, that is, as it is in its wisdom and its inimitability, with the greatness that is Ours, ﴿upon some of the non-Arabs﴾, those who know nothing of the language of the Arabs, from among the animals or the humans. (p-101) The word is the plural of a'jam (ajam), which means one who is not eloquent and has a non-Arabic quality in his speech. Al-a'jami (non-Arab) is like it, with the addition of emphasis through the addition of the nisba ya' (ya' al-nisba).

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 199:**

﴿Then he recited it to them﴾. That is, that which We revealed to him, in its own state of eloquence (*fasaha*) and inimitability (*i'jaz*), while they had certain knowledge that he did not know anything of the language. ﴿They were not believers in it﴾. That is, they were not firmly rooted (in disbelief), and they would contrive an excuse for their disbelief, by calling it sorcery or something else, out of their obstinacy. ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they associate others with Him﴾ [Yusuf: 106], because of the excess of their obstinacy and their readiness and preparation for evil. Indeed, they do not hear it as it should be heard, nor do they comprehend it as it should be comprehended, but (they hear it and understand it) only in a manner that is not its proper way.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 200:

When [that] was a matter of wonder, and it might be that one would suppose the matter was other than its reality, he (al-Biqa'i) established its content and verified it with His saying: ﴿Thus﴾, i.e., like this threading (salk) which is wondrous, which is hearing and outward understanding, in the difficulty of its entry and the narrowness of its passage.

Since the context did not require what the context of al-Hijr required of emphasis, he sufficed with the mere occurrence, and said: ﴿We have threaded it﴾, i.e., Our speech and the truth with which We sent Our messengers, [with what We possess of greatness, into their hearts—this was the original form, but He attached the judgment to the attribute, and generalized it to every time and everyone who is characterized by it, so He said]: ﴿into the hearts of the criminals﴾, i.e., those whom We have sealed upon criminality, which is severance from what ought to be joined, just as the arrow is pierced when shot, or the spear when thrust into the heart, it does not find room in it, nor does it expand with it, but you see it narrow and constricted. (p. 102)

Since this meaning is hidden, he clarified it with His saying: ﴿They do not believe in it﴾, that is, because of the criminality they were created with, and because a seal and sealing were placed upon their hearts, ﴿until they see the painful punishment﴾. Then they will believe at a time when belief will not benefit them, and they will seek safety where there is no safety.

When the coming of evil by surprise is more severe, and its seizing them immediately after they see it, with no respite in which any kind of preparation could take place, he indicated this by depicting its state with His words, using the *fa'* (which signals both greater intensity and *ta'qib*, immediate sequence): ﴿So it will come upon them suddenly﴾.

Since suddenness means coming upon them in heedlessness, he confirmed this, negating any figurative reading, with His words: ﴿while they do not perceive﴾. He also indicated its prolonged presence in their dwellings, its roaming through their midst, and its moving about among their households, with His words, indicating what is more severe for them than being surprised by destruction:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 203:

﴿Then they will say﴾, meaning: in regret, submission and anguish in that state, knowing that there is no way they could withstand it: ﴿Are we to be given respite?﴾, meaning: "Will our lifespans be extended for us, so that we may listen and obey?"

When He had established that their state, at the moment of seizure, was one of pleading in humiliation and abasement [by it], there followed from this the denunciation they deserve for their urgency, in His saying, alerting that His power exceeds description through the nun of majesty (nun al-'azamah, the plural "We" of majesty): ﴿Then is it of Our punishment that they seek to hasten?﴾ That is: and it has become clear to them how His seizing of the earlier nations, the past generations, and the tyrannical peoples was! ﴿They seek to hasten﴾ means: by their saying, "Rain down upon us stones from the sky," "Cause the sky to fall upon us in fragments," "Bring God and the angels before us as a group," just as those people said whose matter We have related and whose mention We have recited, ﴿So cause fragments of the sky to fall upon us﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 26:187], and the like.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 205:

When He had conceived the state of their return, in their being seized by His punishment, [and their urging of it implied mockery, denial, and confidence that they would be left to enjoy themselves, with their hopes attached to their enjoyment lasting a long time; and those who harmed him (ﷺ) wished that it would be hastened for them], Glorified is He, on account of that, made the questioning of their summoner a means of consolation, encouragement and comfort, and so He said: ﴿Have you considered?﴾ meaning: suppose the matter is as they believe, in terms of the length of their life in comfort. Tell Me: ﴿if We let them enjoy for years﴾, meaning in this world, with plentiful living and pure life.

And since the life of the disbeliever is in the utmost narrowness and distress, even if he is in the purest abundance, he expressed it with a form that indicates scarcity, by using the plural of paucity, although the context indicates that it is for abundance; so he said: ﴿years﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 206:

﴿Then there came to them﴾ i.e., after those long years and the prolonged ages, ﴿that which they had been promised﴾ i.e., that of which you had long warned them and cautioned them, bringing it as close to them as possible and making it firmly fixed in their hearing. He informed me.

"What" (ما) — i.e., what thing — ﴿did not avail them﴾, namely, in regard to the punishment that seized them, ﴿what they had been given enjoyment of﴾, that is, a state of the greatest power and long duration, ﴿they were given enjoyment﴾ (p-104), an enjoyment that is in our estimation extremely easy. He portrayed it in the form of something that had existed, as a way of expressing regret over it. The meaning is that it did not avail them anything, because its outcome is destruction; and it increased them in distance from God and His punishment through the increase in sins that necessitate severe retribution.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 208:

Since the implied sense is: "Their gathering of wealth did not avail them anything, because they were not seized except after warners had warned them, through your direct address to them with it, and their hearing of the like of that from those who came before them among the messengers," He connected to it His saying: ﴿And We did not destroy﴾, that is, by Our might, and know that it is by way of comprehensiveness, through His saying: ﴿any town﴾, that is, of the past towns, with the punishment of annihilation, ﴿except that it had warners﴾, their messenger and those who followed him from among his community, and those who heard from the messengers the reports of them together with their peoples from before. He left it without the waw (conjunction) because the situation did not require emphasis, as in al-Hijr, because the warners are witnessed; and if you reflect on the verses of the two passages, that becomes clear to you.

Then he gave the reason for the warning in His saying: ﴿A reminder﴾, meaning: a great alert regarding what it contains of salvation, and a reminding of things they recognize through what their natural dispositions (fitar) of intellect led them to, and what the insights of their hearts guided them to. He made the warners themselves the reminder, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah has indeed sent down to you a reminder﴾ [al-Talaq: 10], ﴿a Messenger﴾ [al-Talaq: 11]. This is an indication of their thoroughness in reminding, to the point that they became the reminder itself.

Since the implied meaning is: "We did not destroy any town from among them except with truth," He joined to it His saying: ﴿And We were not﴾ (p-105) — or the waw is for the circumstantial (hal) from the nun of "ahlaknā" (We destroyed) — ﴿wrongdoers﴾, meaning: in destroying any of them, because they disbelieved in Our blessing and worshipped other than Us, after the warning had been given to them, the proofs had followed one another, and the threats had been continuously delivered.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 210:

When He (subhanahu) informed that the ultimate purpose of the sending down of this Qur'an was that he (ﷺ) should be one of the warners, and followed that with what suits it, until He concluded with the destruction of those who denied the warners, He conjoined to His saying ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 193] His saying, as an indication that care is intense in this context regarding the Qur'an, in order to establish that it is from Allah, and He negated any confusion about it by His saying ﴿Nor have the devils brought it down﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿the devils﴾, i.e., so that it would be sorcery, or soothsaying, or poetry, or confused dreams, as they say.

Since the absence of engaging in the act does not necessarily entail the absence of fitness for it, He said: ﴿And it does not befit them﴾, i.e., it is not valid, and it is not conceivable from them, that they should descend with any of it, because it is entirely good and blessing, whereas they are the source of evil and destruction. Between the two there is complete contrast: you are tranquility and light, while they are upheaval and perdition. So there is no approach for them toward you, and no way at all to you.

Since the absence of that negation does not necessarily entail the absence of capacity on their part, He said: ﴿And they are not able﴾, i.e., to descend with it, even if their efforts to achieve it intensify, on the assumption that they have some receptiveness to that;

Then he gave the reason for this with His words: ﴿Indeed, they are removed from hearing﴾, that is, (p-106) from the Perfect Truth, from the Exalted Assembly (al-Mala' al-A'la), ﴿they are indeed removed﴾, that is, by what the heavens were protected with from the meteors, and by what they were separated from the angels with in reality, because the angels are pure goodness and unmixed light, whereas these (the devils) are utter evil and pure darkness. So they hear only by snatching, and then, through what occurs to their understandings and is imagined in their illusions by way of imagination, it becomes a mixture most of which has no reality, so that nothing of its majority can be trusted. It is not far-fetched that this applies generally, so that it includes hearing from believers, because they share with the angels in light and goodness. Consider what has been reported regarding "Ayat al-Kursi," that it is not recited in a house but that a devil comes near it, and in another narration: "except that the devil leaves it." A similar report came concerning the last two verses of Surat al-Baqarah, and likewise whatever is of similar forms. Greater than all of this is his saying, may the prayers and peace of Allah be upon him, to 'Umar (radiya Allahu 'anhu): "Indeed, O son of al-Khattab, by Him in whose hand is my soul, the devil never met you traveling a path except that he took a path other than your path." He left out the explanation of the ambiguity (al-infibaa'), because it is evident.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 213:

Since its implied sense is that they call upon the false idols (ṭawāghīt), while the Qur'an calls to God, the True, the Manifest, He causally connected to it His saying: ﴿So do not call upon⦆ another god ⦅with God⦆... Here He addressed His Prophet, upon whom be blessings and peace, who is the most honoured of creation in His sight and the dearest of them to Him, so that this would be a gentle lesson for others regarding the warning that comes to them, and so that the threat would be a stronger deterrent for them, and they would be more receptive to it. ﴿With God⦆ means: the One who possesses every perfection, the One to whom this Qur'an, which the Trustworthy Spirit (al-Rūḥ al-Amīn) brought down upon you, calls, because of the complete affinity between you and them in luminosity and goodness. ﴿Another god⦆ — the wisdom of bringing the phrase ﴿another⦆ ... ﴿so you would be⦆ was discussed at the end of Surat al-Furqan. That is, as a consequence of that, you would be ﴿among those punished⦆, from the One who is capable of whatever He wills with the utmost ease and facility. This statement is for everyone who hears the Qur'an, urging them to reflect upon its meaning, its purpose and its aim, so that it may be known that it is in the utmost contrast with the devils and their misguidance, and in harmony with the drawn-near ones and their states. Perhaps He addressed it to the Infallible (al-Ma'ṣūm) to increase the exhortation to follow guidance and avoid ruin, and so that His saying would be connected to it.

﴿And warn﴾, that is, with this Qur'an, ﴿your tribe﴾, that is, your clan, ﴿the closest of kin﴾, that is, those nearest to you in lineage. Do not show favor to anyone, for the greatest purpose of warning is to restrain creatures from what leads to ruin, namely following the devils, who lured them away from their religion after they had all been ḥunafā' (upright monotheists). Warning the nearest of kin conveys the warning to others by way of a fortiori reasoning (min bāb al-awlā, "from the door of what is more fitting"). It also breaks the pride of the more distant from confronting what he dislikes, because the Prophet took the path of the nearest. The Prophet (ﷺ) fulfilled this verse in the fullest sense. Al-Bukhārī narrated from Ibn 'Abbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "When it was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) went up onto al-Ṣafā and began calling out: 'O Banū Fihr! [O Banū 'Adī!]' to the clans of Quraysh, until they gathered. A man who could not come out would send a messenger to see what it was. Abū Lahab and Quraysh came, and he said: 'Tell me, if I informed you that a cavalry was in the valley intending to raid you, would you believe me?' They said: 'Yes! We have never known you to tell anything but the truth.' He said: 'Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment.' Abū Lahab said: 'May you perish all day! Did you gather us for this?' Then it was revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abū Lahab, and perish he﴾ [al-Masad: 1]." In another narration, he (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of Quraysh! Save yourselves, for I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O Banū 'Abd Manāf! I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O 'Abbās ibn 'Abd al-Muṭṭalib! I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O Ṣafiyyah, aunt of the Messenger of Allah! I cannot avail you anything against Allah. O Fāṭimah, daughter of Muḥammad! Ask me for whatever you wish of my wealth; I cannot avail you anything against Allah." Abū Ya'lā narrated the account from al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwām, may Allah be pleased with him, that "Quraysh came to him, and he warned and admonished them. They asked him for the signs of Sulaymān with the wind, of Dāwūd with the mountains, of Mūsā with the sea, and of 'Īsā in raising the dead, and that he should make the mountains move, cause the rivers to gush forth, and turn the rock into gold. Allah revealed to him while they were with him, and when it was lifted from him he informed them that he had been given what they asked, but that if he showed it to them and they disbelieved, they would be hastened to punishment." So he (ﷺ) chose [patience] with them, so that Allah might admit them through the gate of mercy.

Since warning (al-nidhara) is only directed at those who turn away, He commanded its opposite for its opposites, saying: ﴿And lower your wing﴾, i.e., be utmost in gentleness. That is because when a bird wishes to rise, it raises its wings, and when it wishes to descend, it folds and lowers them; so He made this an example of humility ﴿to those who follow you﴾. Perhaps by expressing it with the form of ittafala (the reflexive form, meaning "to follow" with effort and willingness), he guarded against cases like Abu Talib, who did not believe, or who believed outwardly while being a hypocrite, or who was weak in faith and a wrongdoer (fasiq). He confirmed the intended meaning by His saying: ﴿of the believers﴾, i.e., those for whom faith has become a firmly established quality, whether they were among the closest (of your kin) or the more distant.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar, *The Arrangement of Pearls*) on surah 26, verse 216:

When this made clear that this ruling applies generally to all their conditions, he continued with his words: ﴿But if they disobey you﴾, meaning: they, and so others [by way of a fortiori], ﴿then say﴾, meaning: abandoning the manner in which you dealt with them while they were believers, in leniency: ﴿Indeed, I am free﴾, meaning: completely disassociated ﴿from what you do﴾, meaning: from the disobedience about which the Qur'an has warned. He singled out the believers, to elevate their rank, by increasing their honour, so that this would inform that troubled one of the knowledge of his state, which would then urge him to join them.

When this verse was made known, requiring the rejection of whoever disobeys, whoever he may be, even if he was one who had shown firm establishment in faith, because of the great submission (idhan) that was seen in him, He followed it with His saying: ﴿And put your trust﴾ [i.e.: ] in your protection, your deliverance, and the turning of (p-١١٠) the warners toward obedience. The reading of the people of Madina and Syria with the causal fa' (fa' al-sababiyyah, the "fa'" of causation) is more indicative of this. ﴿in the Mighty﴾, i.e., the One able to repel [harm] from you and to take vengeance upon them, ﴿the Merciful﴾, i.e., the One hoped for to honour all of them by removing opposition and enmity, and to bring them happiness by employing them in what pleases Him.

Then he followed the command to rely upon Him (tawakkul) with a description that entails sufficiency in everything that befalls one, in warding off harm and bringing about benefit. That is the all-encompassing knowledge (al-'ilm al-muhit) which entails all the attributes of perfection. So He said: ﴿Who sees you﴾, that is, with sight and knowledge, ﴿when you stand up﴾ from your sleep, from your bed, leaving off your inclination, for the sake of [the good pleasure of] your Lord.

"And" [He sees] ﴿your movement﴾ in prayer, prostrating and standing, ﴿among those who prostrate﴾, i.e., among the praying believers who follow you. There is a humming of the Qur'an from you like the humming of bees, humility out of fear of God, supplication, sighs rising up, and weeping. [That is:] He is worthy of your turning to Him and your submission before Him, that they should love you with everything that pleases you.

Since these states encompass speech, and He had mentioned seeing, which includes knowledge, He explained that by stating it explicitly coupled with hearing, saying: ﴿Indeed, He is﴾ that is, He alone, ﴿the All-Hearing﴾ that is, of all your utterances, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ that is, of everything you conceal and reveal of your deeds. It has been mentioned more than once before that the comprehensiveness of knowledge (p-111) entails the perfection of power, so it is as if He had said: Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, the All-Seeing, the All-Powerful, confirming the one who relies upon Him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 26, verse 221:

When Glorified is He had explained that the Qur'an is contrary to the statements of the devils (shayatin), and explained that the state of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the state of his followers are contrary to their states and the states of those who come to them, the soothsayers (kuhhan), by what He mentioned of the Prophet's (ﷺ) action and the action of his partisans, may Allah be pleased with them, in turning to Allah and turning away from everything else, it became known that between them and them there is a great distance and a great and severe difference, and that the state of the Prophet (ﷺ) is in agreement with the state of the Trustworthy Spirit (Jibril), who descended upon him with the Wise Reminder. The soul yearned to know the states of the brethren of the devils. So He said, stirring up whoever wishes that, and completing the removal of confusion about the Qur'an being from Allah, and a distinction between the verses that are burdened with that for the sake of praising their mention and alerting to the emphasis of their matter: ﴿Shall I inform you﴾, that is: I will inform you of a momentous report, beneficial in the religion, of great benefit in distinguishing [between] the friends of the Most Merciful and the brethren of Satan ﴿upon whom do the devils descend﴾ and frequent ﴿the devils﴾ when they eavesdrop, in a manner of concealment, by which the deletion of the ta' has signified, and the preposition ('ala) entered upon the noun that includes interrogation, (p-112) because the meaning of inclusion is that its original form was: amana (from 'amman), so the hamzah was deleted from it by a continuous deletion, as was done in "hal" because its original form was "ahal," as he said:

Ask the horsemen of Yarbu', by our severity, the people who saw us at the slope of the flat plain, the one with the dunes.

So the interrogation is implied before the preposition, as al-Zamakhshari stated.

Now that it is as if it had been said, "Yes, inform us!", He said: ﴿The devils descend﴾ gradually and repeatedly ﴿upon every lying (affaka) sinner﴾, that is, one who turns matters from their proper aspects through falsehood, slander, deception and transgression, of the class of soothsayers and associates of the jinn, ﴿sinful (athim)﴾, one who commits sins with the utmost effort. These are the sinners.

The devils ﴿cast their hearing﴾ to the devils, and they listen to them with the utmost attentiveness, because of the affinity between them, through their common trait of spreading falsehood without concern or restraint. Or the devils convey what they overhear, which they steal by listening to the angels, to their allies, so they speak of what they have heard from them and mix in what their own souls have adorned for them. ﴿And most of them are liars﴾, that is, both groups, in what they relay of the reports of what they hear, of the mixing that occurred in what reached them, and of the fabrications and confusion they added, out of their absorption in the desire for knowledge of the unseen, which leads to falsehood and error. (p-113) Al-Razi said in *al-Lawami'*, in substance, that wherever there is rectitude in the state of the imagination (that is, the imaginative faculty, *al-quwwa al-mutakhayyila*), it is the abode of the angels, and wherever there is crookedness in the state of the imagination, it is the dwelling place of the devils. Whoever is suited to the spiritual beings among the angels, their descent upon him, their appearing to him, their influence upon him, and their taking on forms [in him] will occur, so that when they appear upon him, he speaks with their speech and they speak with his tongue, he sees with their eyes and they see with his eyes; they are angels walking on the earth at peace. ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, the angels descend upon them﴾ [Fussilat: 30]. And whoever is suited to the devils, from among the satans, their descent upon him, their appearing to him, [their influence upon him], and their taking on forms in him, [so that when they appear upon him, he speaks with their speech and they speak with his tongue, he sees with their eyes and they see] with his eyes, are the devils of mankind walking on the earth as corrupters. The end.

When al-Biqa'i's point was established—by distancing it from the ranks of the devils and elevating it to the ranks of the spiritual beings, namely the honored angels who come from the Lord of the worlds—that it is magic, and that it is confused dreams and fabrication, the Glorified One denied that it is poetry by His saying: ﴿And the poets—the misguided follow them﴾. That is, with the utmost effort, in the reading of other than Nafi' with the doubled consonant (yattabi'uhum, meaning they follow them intensively), because of their admiration for their speech and conduct, so they learn from them and transmit from them. ﴿The misguided﴾ means those who go astray, who incline away from the most upright way toward fornication, obscenity, and every corruption that drags one to ruin. And they, as you see, are far from the followers of Muhammad (ﷺ), with whom Allah is pleased, the prostrating, weeping, ascetic ones.

Now that he had established the condition of their followers, from which it is known that they (the poets) are more misguided than them, because of their indulgence in the desire for glib chatter with the tongue, to the point that falsehood and slander seemed good to them, he indicated this by His saying: ﴿Have you not seen that they﴾, i.e., the poets, and He portrayed their state by His saying: ﴿in every valley﴾, i.e., of the valleys of speech, of praise, satire, amatory verse (nasib), elegy (ritha'), boasting (hamasa), obscenity (mujun) and other than these, ﴿they wander﴾, i.e., they travel like the bewildered wanderer, confused and deviating from the path of truth, wherever speech drags them they are dragged along: into defaming lineages, into erotic verse (tashbib) about the women of honour (huram), into satire, and into praising those who do not deserve praise, and the like. For this reason He said:

The Qur'an, 26:226: "And that they say what they do not do."

That is: because they did not intend it, and the art they followed (al-fann alladhi salakuhu) compelled them to it. Most of their statements have no realities behind them. Look at the Maqamat of al-Hariri (the Maqamat, a work of rhymed prose narratives) and the tales he fabricated in them, and the marvelous matters he invented that have no realities. The people of ittihad (ittihad, the doctrine of union with God) made these the basis of their heretical innovation (bid'ah) and the foundation of their losing bargain. How he exposed their condition and made their misguidance clear!

This is unlike the Qur'an, for it contains sublime meanings that are verified, in sound and beautiful well-arranged words, and in inimitable, overwhelming styles and marvelously firm compositions, with no artificiality in any of them. Thus no one of sound disposition turns away from it. The result is that none follows them in their affair except a deviator like them, and none renounces this Qur'an except one whose nature is coarse and whose heart is dark and gloomy.

(p. 116) Since poetry, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said, contains wisdom (ḥikmah), and since, as ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said, it stands in relation to speech generally as speech does, with good and bad in it, and since among the poets there were those who praised Islam and the Muslims, satirised polytheism and the polytheists, encouraged detachment from this world and desire for the Hereafter, urged noble character, and warned against its vices, the distinguishing factor between the praiseworthy and the blameworthy kind was the frequent remembrance of Allah. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Except those who believe﴾, that is, in Allah and His Messenger, ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾, that is, confirming their faith by action, ﴿the righteous deeds﴾, that is, those which Allah and His Messenger have prescribed for them, ﴿and remember Allah often﴾, keeping in mind His perfection, ﴿often﴾. Poetry did not distract them from remembrance; rather they built their poetry upon the matters of religion and the defence of the Shariah, so that all of this became remembrance of Allah. A sufficient example of this is the ode attributed to Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) and its reply by Ibn al-Zibaʿrā, who was then still upon his polytheism. This took place at the first military expedition (sariyyah) in Islam, which was the expedition of ʿUbaydah ibn al-Ḥārith [ibn al-Muṭṭalib ibn ʿAbd Manāf] (may Allah be pleased with him). Indeed, there is no line in Abu Bakr's ode (may Allah be pleased with him) that does not contain the remembrance of Allah, either explicitly or by mention of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) or something of his religion. Whatever line lacks any of that is nonetheless inclined toward it, being built upon it. As for its opposite, there is nothing of that kind in it. Ibn Isḥāq said: Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said concerning the expedition of ʿUbaydah ibn al-Ḥārith (may Allah be pleased with him):

Has the phantom of Salmā at al-Biṭāḥ al-Damāʾith kept you awake, and does news pass among the clan?
A group from Luʾayy that no warning turns from disbelief, nor does any summoner rouse them,
A truthful messenger came to them, and they called him a liar and said, "You shall not remain among us,"
When we call them to the truth they turn their backs and snarl like hounds, panting in their pens.
How often have we been bound to them by kinship, and what remains of piety for them is but a ruin that does not fall.
So if they return from their disbelief and their disobedience to parents, [we will answer]; and if they persist in their insolence and error,
Then the good things of what is lawful are not like the foul things, and the punishment of Allah will not be far from them.
We are men from the summit of Ghālib, to whom belongs the glory among its uppermost branches.
So let the Lord of the dancing maidens at evening be the first to answer, with swift she-camels that stride on the rough ground,
Like the dark-eyed gazelles about Mecca in devotion, coming to the wells' basins, licking at the thirst-quenching water.
If they do not soon return from their error, and I have sworn an oath in speech, I am not one who breaks it,
Then a raid will surely fall upon them, bearing a truthful report, that forbids the chaste women their menstrual impurity.
It will leave their dead in heaps, around which the birds circle, and the disbelievers will show no more mercy than the son of Ḥārith.
So convey to Banū Sahm, with you there, a message, and every ingrate who seeks evil is a seeker.
If you rise against my honour in your evil opinion, then I am not one who fails to defend your honour.

Ibn al-Zibaʿrā replied to him, saying:

Is it from the traces of a dwelling deserted at al-ʿAthāʿith that you wept with an eye whose tears do not cease?
And of the wonders of the days and of all time, there is a wonder concerning the successive and the recurring events:
An army came upon us, fierce, led by ʿUbaydah, who in the clamour is called the son of Ḥārith,
That we might leave idols at Mecca devoted, inheritances from a noble ancestor to his heirs.
When we met them with spears of Radīnah wood, and swift steeds, noble, panting in the dust,
And white swords, as if salt were upon their backs, in the hands of warriors like lions that rend.
We set up with them a whirlwind that did not waver, and we quenched our vengeance swiftly without delay.
So they retreated in great fear and dread, and a matter that was delayed seemed to them wondrous.
Had they not done so, women would have wailed, widows of theirs, between the one who had lost her menstrual cycle and the one who had menstruated.
The dead were left behind, of whom one who knows them well or a heedless one who does not seek will tell.
So convey, to Abu Bakr at your place, a message: you are not one who will remain against the honour of Fihr.
And since you have not been bound by me to a solemn oath that renews war, whose sworn word is not broken.

Al-Baghawī narrated with his chain, through ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from the hadith of Kaʿb ibn Mālik (may Allah be pleased with him), that he said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Allah has revealed concerning poetry what He has revealed." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the believer strives with his sword and his tongue. By Him in whose hand is my soul, it is as if you are shooting them with it, a spray of arrows." Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) used to recite poetry and ask others to recite it in the mosque. Imam Aḥmad narrated the hadith of Kaʿb, and al-Nasāʾī narrated, through narrators on whom Muslim relied, from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Strive against the polytheists with your wealth, your lives, and your tongues." Al-Baghawī said: It is related that he, that is Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both), summoned ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿah al-Makhzūmī, and asked him to recite the ode he had composed:

Are you departing in the morning from the family of Nuʿmā, or setting out in the evening, travelling by day?

It is about ninety lines. When he finished it, Ibn ʿAbbās repeated it back, having memorised it after a single hearing. For the poet, to escape the blame of this verse, it is enough that poetry does not so overwhelm him that it distracts him from remembrance, to the point of his being among those who go astray. It is not a condition that his poetry contain no frivolity at all. Ḥassān (may Allah be pleased with him) used to recite to the Prophet (ﷺ) lines like his words in a long ode in which he praised him (ﷺ):

As if a cup from the house of Ras, its mixture honey and water,
When the wine-cups are mentioned on a day, they are the ransom for the goodness of the wine,
We ascribe to it the blame if we are at fault, when there is a striking or a striking back,
And we drink it, and it leaves us kings and lions whom the encounter does not repel.

The prohibition of wine was in the third or fourth year after the Hijrah. This ode Ḥassān (may Allah be pleased with him) composed at the Conquest in the eighth year, or at the ʿUmrat al-Qaḍāʾ in the seventh year. So it is among the things in which the poet says what he does not do.

When the Glorified had described the state of those excepted in the remembrance, which is the foundation of every matter, He followed it with what drove them to poetry of the injustice that gave them hope of victory, saying: ﴿And who defend themselves﴾, that is, they undertook for themselves the means of victory through their poetry against those who harmed them, ﴿after they had been wronged﴾, that is, after the injustice of the wrongdoer had befallen them through satire or the like.

When the Glorified permitted defence against the wrongdoer, and the one who begins, if he confines the responder to his reply, is unjust, while if he exceeds the limit he is deserving of transgressing and regretting it, Allah warned both, emphasising the threat with the particle "sa-" in His saying, which the righteous predecessors (al-salaf al-ṣāliḥ) used to admonish one another with, for you will find nothing more awe-inspiring than it, nor more terrifying, nor more painful to the hearts of the reflective, nor more shattering to the livers of those who contemplate: ﴿And those who have done wrong will know﴾, and by generalisation in His saying ﴿those who have done wrong﴾, that is all of them, whoever they were, [and] by terror through indefiniteness in His saying ﴿what a return they will return﴾, that is, in this world and the Hereafter. Its end has been linked, as you see, to the description of the Clear Book with what it was described with of majesty and greatness, that it is from [the presence of] Allah, sent down with the Trustworthy Spirit, upon the best of His creatures, removing every confusion and negating all falsehood from it. It is concluded with a threat against wrongdoing at its beginning, in the glorification of the Clear Book, consolation for the Noble Prophet (ﷺ), and a warning to the disbelievers who are the greatest of wrongdoers. What followed it connected with describing the Clear Qur'an, glad tidings for the believers and a warning to the disbelievers. So glorified is He who sent it down upon the unlettered, trustworthy Prophet, as guidance for the worlds, and as a clear sign through its inimitability to all creatures, remaining until the Day of Religion.
